topic: Competition Organisation — General Principles
text:
A Competition is reserved for Formula One Cars as defined in the Technical Regulations. Each Competition will have the status of an international restricted competition. A Competition may be cancelled if fewer than twelve (12) Cars are available for it.

A Competition commences four (4) hours before FP1 is scheduled to start and ends at the time for the lodging of a protest under the terms of the ISC Code, or the time when a technical or sporting certification has been carried out under the terms of the ISC Code, whichever is the later.

The stewards or Race Director may give instructions to Competitors by means of special circulars in accordance with the Code. All classifications and results of free practice, sprint qualifying, sprint session, qualifying, and the Race, as well as all decisions issued by officials, will be published using the Document Management System. Any decision or communication concerning a particular Competitor should be given to them within twenty-five (25) minutes.

Unless written FIA permission is given, the circuit may only be used for purposes other than the Competition after the last practice session on each day of practice, after Qualifying the Sprint (where scheduled), and on the day of the Race no less than one (1) hour before the end of the Pit Lane is opened to allow F1 Cars to cover a reconnaissance lap.

Competitors are not permitted to attempt to alter the grip of any part of the track surface (other than by driving on the track). The Race Director, Chief Medical Officer (CMO), or Medical Delegate can require a driver to have a medical examination at any time during a Competition. If the Impact Warning Light is activated after an incident, the driver may be required to be examined by the Competition medical service without delay.

topic: FIA Delegates
text:
For each Competition the FIA will nominate the following mandatory delegates: Safety Delegate, Medical Delegate, Technical Delegate, and Media Delegate. The FIA may also nominate: a representative of the President of the FIA, a Deputy Race Director, a Deputy Medical Delegate, an Observer, a Safety Car driver, and a medical car driver.

The role of FIA delegates is to help officials of the Competition in their duties, to see within their fields of competence that all the Regulations governing the Championship are respected, to make any comments they judge necessary, and to draw up any necessary reports concerning the Competition.

The Technical Delegate nominated by the FIA is responsible for scrutineering. The Technical Delegate may carry out, or have carried out by scrutineers, at their discretion, any checks to verify the compliance of the F1 Cars entered in the Competition, at any time until the end of the Competition, without prior request from the stewards or clerk of the course. The Technical Delegate has full authority over the national scrutineers.

topic: Officials — Stewards, Race Director, Clerk of Course
text:
From among holders of an FIA Super Licence, the following officials will be nominated by the FIA: a minimum of three and a maximum of four stewards (one appointed chair), a Race Director, and a Permanent Starter.

From among holders of an FIA Super Licence, the following officials will be nominated by the ASN: one steward from among the ASN nationals and the clerk of the course.

The Clerk of the Course shall work in permanent consultation with the Race Director. The Race Director shall have overriding authority over: (a) control of free practice, qualifying, sprint qualifying, sprint session and the Race, including timetable adherence; (b) stopping any F1 Car; (c) stopping free practice/qualifying/sprint qualifying, suspension of sprint or Race if unsafe; (d) the starting procedure; (e) use of the Safety Car.

The stewards, Race Director, Clerk of the Course, and Technical Delegate must be present at the start of the Competition. In exceptional circumstances, stewards not present at the start must be available and contactable at all times. The Race Director must be in radio contact with the clerk of the course and chairman of Stewards at all times when F1 Cars are permitted to run on the track. The Clerk of the Course must be in Race control and in radio contact with all marshal's posts during these times. The Stewards may use any video or electronic means to assist them in reaching a decision and may overrule judges of fact.

topic: Official Meetings
text:
At each Alternative Format Competition (AFC — where a sprint session is scheduled), meetings chaired by the Race Director will take place: three (3) hours before the start of FP1 (attended by all team managers), one (1) hour after the end of FP1 (attended by all drivers and team managers), and one and a half (1.5) hours after the end of the Sprint Qualifying session (attended by all drivers and team managers).

At each Standard Format Competition (SFC — no sprint), meetings chaired by the Race Director will take place: three (3) hours before the start of FP1 (attended by all team managers) and one and a half (1.5) hours after the end of FP2 (attended by all drivers and team managers).

Should the Race Director consider another meeting necessary, it will take place three (3) hours before the start of the Race. Competitors will be informed no later than five (5) hours before the start of the Race. All drivers and team managers must attend.

topic: General Safety — Track and Pit Lane
text:
Pit Lane and track discipline and safety measures are the same for all free practice sessions, the qualifying session, the sprint qualifying session, and sprint session as for the Race, unless the Sporting Regulations require otherwise.

If an F1 Car stops on the track, it shall be the duty of the marshals to remove it as quickly as possible so that its presence does not constitute a danger or hinder other Competitors. Under no circumstances may a driver stop their F1 Car on the track without justifiable reason.

No one except the driver may touch a stopped F1 Car unless it is in the paddock, the Competitor's Designated Garage Area, the Pit Lane, or on the starting grid (save as specifically authorised by the ISC Code or Sporting Regulations).

During the period commencing fifteen (15) minutes prior to and ending five (5) minutes after every free practice session, qualifying session, and sprint qualifying session, and the period between the commencement of the formation lap preceding the sprint session and the Race and the time when the last F1 Car enters the parc fermé, no one is allowed on the track, the Pit Entry Road, or the Pit Exit Road. Exceptions: marshals/authorised personnel in execution of duty; drivers (driving or on foot with marshal permission); F1 Team personnel when pushing a car or clearing equipment from the grid after all cars able to do so have left on the formation lap; F1 Team personnel when assisting marshals to remove a car from the grid after the start of the TTCS.

topic: Car Safety Lights
text:
Rear Lights: The rear lights described in Article C14.3 must be illuminated at all times when using intermediate or wet-weather tyres. All rear lights must be in working order when the F1 Car leaves the Pit Lane for the first time for any LTCS or TTCS. It shall be at the discretion of the Race Director to decide whether or not a driver should be stopped if the central rear light (Article C14.3.2) and at least one of the side lights (Article C14.3.3) are not working. Should an F1 Car be stopped in this way the driver may re-join when the fault has been remedied.

Lateral Lights: The lateral lights described in Article C14.7 must be in working order when the F1 Car leaves the Pit Lane for the first time for any LTCS or TTCS.

topic: General Safety — Fire Extinguishers, Animals, Signalling Area
text:
The organiser must make at least two (2) fire extinguishers of 5kg capacity available to each Competitor and ensure that they work properly.

Animals, except those which may have been expressly authorised by the FIA for use by security services, are forbidden on the track, in the Pit Lane, in the paddock, or in any spectator area.

Only twelve (12) team members for each Competitor are permitted in the signalling area during any free practice session, qualifying session, sprint qualifying session, sprint session, and the Race.

topic: Refuelling Rules
text:
Refuelling is only permitted in the Competitors' designated garages. No F1 Car may be refuelled, nor may fuel be removed from an F1 Car, at a rate greater than 0.8 litres per second. The driver may remain in their F1 Car throughout refuelling, but the engine must be stopped.

During all refuelling or fuel handling operations: (i) relevant personnel must wear outer garments complying with FIA Standard 8867-2016, FIA Standard 8856-2000, or FIA Standard 8856-2018; (ii) an assistant equipped with a suitable fire extinguisher of appropriate capacity must be present wearing compliant outer garments; (iii) all F1 Cars, refuelling equipment and containers must be suitably grounded where necessary; (iv) any powered pumping system used to transfer fuel must be operated by a non-latching switch or be turned off automatically if the operator leaves.

topic: Heat Hazard
text:
If the Official Weather Service predicts that the Heat Index will be greater than 31.0°C at some time during the Sprint or the Race at a Competition, or at the sole discretion of the Race Director, a "Heat Hazard" may be declared twenty-four (24) hours prior to the scheduled start of the Competition. Once declared, it remains in force for the Competition. All Competitors will be notified via the official messaging system.

Once a Heat Hazard is declared: (a) All components of the Driver Cooling System, except cooling medium and items of driver personal equipment forming part of the system, must be fitted. (b) At the start of any Sprint session or Race for which a Heat Hazard has been declared, all components of the Driver Cooling System must be fitted, functional, and available for use by the driver meeting Article C14.6.1 provisions. However, any driver may elect not to wear personal equipment forming part of the Driver Cooling System — in such case all other components including cooling medium must be fitted, and the difference in mass between the driver's personal equipment normally used and the system equipment must be compensated by 0.5kg of ballast in the cockpit (included in Article C4.6b sum of masses). (c) The Heat Hazard Mass Increase shall apply in accordance with Articles C4.1 and C4.6.

topic: Rain Hazard
text:
If the Official Weather Service predicts that the probability of precipitation is greater than 40% at some point during the Sprint or the Race at a Competition, or at the sole discretion of the Race Director, a "Rain Hazard" may be declared.

At each AFC (Alternative Format Competition), a Rain Hazard will be declared for the Sprint no later than two (2) hours before the start of Sprint Qualifying; it remains in force from the time of declaration until the end-of-session signal for the Sprint is given.

At all Competitions, a Rain Hazard will be declared for the Race no later than two (2) hours before the start of Qualifying; it remains in force from the time of declaration until the end-of-session signal for the Race is given.

When an F1 Car is deemed to be in parc fermé whilst a Rain Hazard is in force, other than when the F1 Cars are sealed in accordance with Article B3.4.2 or B3.4.3, the work described in FIA-F1-DOC-080 may be carried out.

topic: Pit Lane — Designated Garage Areas
text:
The FIA will allocate garages and an area in the Pit Lane on an equal basis where each Competitor may work, with one position for pit stops during any session within each Designated Garage Area.

Competitors may NOT: (a) paint lines on any part of the Pit Lane; (b) attempt to enhance the grip of the surface in the Pit Lane, other than by drying, sweeping, or by laying tyre rubber when F1 Cars leave their pit stop position, unless a problem has been clearly identified and a solution agreed to by the Race Director; (c) leave equipment in the Fast Lane (except as detailed in Article B5.3); (d) use any powered device to lift any part of an F1 Car in the Pit Lane; (e) carry out work on an F1 Car anywhere other than the Inner Lane (except when F1 Cars are at the end of the Pit Lane per Articles B5.3 and B5.14), though no work may be carried out in the Fast Lane if it is likely to hinder other F1 Cars attempting to leave the Pit Lane.

topic: Pit Lane Safety — Car Release
text:
An F1 Car will be deemed to have been released from the Competitors' Designated Garage Area either when it has been driven out of its Designated Garage Area when leaving from the garage, or after the rear axle has passed the position occupied by the front axle when it was stationary following a pit stop. Competitors must provide a means of clearly establishing when an F1 Car was released, viewable from both above and in front of the F1 Car.

F1 Cars must not be released from a garage or pit stop position in any way that could endanger Pit Lane personnel or another driver, or likely to cause damage to another car. F1 Cars must not be released in an unsafe condition.

If released in an unsafe condition during any LTCS: stewards may drop the driver such number of grid positions as considered appropriate (applied to the Race, or to the sprint if during sprint qualifying). If released in an unsafe condition during a TTCS: a Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed; if the driver retires from the TTCS as a result, a fine may be imposed on the Competitor. An additional penalty will be imposed on any driver who, in the opinion of the stewards, continues to drive an F1 Car knowing it to have been released in an unsafe condition.

F1 Team personnel are only allowed in the Pit Lane immediately before they are required to work on an F1 Car and must withdraw as soon as the work is complete.

topic: Pit Lane Safety — Helmets and Personnel
text:
All team personnel carrying out any work on an F1 Car in the Pit Lane when the F1 Car is in its pit stop position for the purpose of adjusting or replacing components, or serving a penalty during the qualifying session, the sprint qualifying session, or a TTCS, must be wearing helmets which meet or exceed the requirements of ECE 22.05 (European motorcycle road helmet), DOT (USA motorcycle road helmet), or JIS T8133-2015 class 2 (JPN protective helmets for automobile users). The use of appropriate eye protection is compulsory.

Unless authorised by the FIA, no one under the age of 16 is permitted in the Pit Lane during: (i) the period commencing fifteen (15) minutes prior to and ending five (5) minutes after every free practice session, the qualifying session, and the sprint qualifying session; (ii) the period commencing fifteen (15) minutes before the pit exit is opened to allow F1 Cars to cover reconnaissance laps and the time when the last F1 Car enters the parc fermé after the TTCS has ended.

topic: Pit Lane — Speed Limits and Driving Rules
text:
A speed limit of 80km/h will be imposed in the Pit Lane during the whole Competition. This limit may be amended by the Race Director to ensure safe and orderly conduct.

Speed limit violations: During any free practice session, qualifying, or sprint qualifying, a Competitor whose driver exceeds the limit will be fined €100 for each km/h above the limit, up to a maximum of €1000. The stewards may impose an additional penalty if they suspect a driver was speeding in order to gain advantage. During a TTCS, the stewards may impose a 5-Second Penalty, 10-Second Penalty, Drive-Through Penalty, or Stop-and-Go Penalty.

At no time may an F1 Car be reversed in the Pit Lane under its own power.

No F1 Car should be driven from its pit stop position unless: (i) it has first been driven into the pit stop position having just entered the Pit Lane from the track; and (ii) it is then driven immediately back onto the track from the pit stop position.

Unless pushed from the grid during the start procedure, F1 Cars may only be driven from the Competitors' Designated Garage Area to the end of the Pit Lane. Any car(s) driven to the end of the Pit Lane prior to the start or re-start of a LTCS must form up in a line in the Fast Lane and leave in the order they got there unless another F1 Car is unduly delayed.

There will be a green and a red light at the end of the Pit Lane. F1 Cars may only be driven out when the light is green. A blue flag and/or flashing blue light will be shown in the Pit Exit Road to warn drivers leaving the Pit Lane if F1 Cars are approaching on the track.

topic: Pit Lane — Closing
text:
In exceptional circumstances the Race Director may ask for the pit entry to be closed for safety reasons. At such times drivers may only enter the Pit Lane in order for essential and entirely evident repairs to be carried out to their F1 Car.

During a LTCS, a penalty in accordance with Article B1.9.4 may be imposed on any driver who, in the opinion of the stewards, entered the Pit Lane without justifiable reason whilst it was closed.

During a TTCS, a Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who, in the opinion of the stewards, entered the Pit Lane for any other reason whilst it was closed.

topic: Changes of Driver
text:
During a Championship each Competitor will be permitted to use a maximum of four (4) drivers in Races, and any new driver may score points in the Championship.

Provided any change proposed after the end of initial scrutineering receives the consent of the stewards, a change of driver may be made: (a) At each Competition where a sprint session is not scheduled, at any time before the start of the qualifying session; (b) At each Competition where a sprint session is scheduled, at any time before the start of the sprint qualifying session (for a driver who will participate in the sprint session), or at any time before the start of the qualifying session (for a driver who will participate in the Race). Additional changes for reasons of force majeure will be considered separately.

Each Competitor will be permitted to use additional drivers during FP1 and FP2, provided that: (a) The FIA are informed which F1 Cars and drivers each Competitor intends to use in each session no less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 (any changes less than two (2) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 may only be made with the consent of the stewards); (b) No more than two (2) drivers are used in any one (1) session; (c) On two (2) Competitions during the Championship, for each F1 Car entered for the Championship, each Competitor must use a driver who has not participated in more than two (2) Championship Races in their career. The Competitor must inform the FIA in writing seven (7) days prior to the start of the relevant Competition with: (i) the details of the rookie driver; (ii) which of the Competitor's entered F1 Cars this driver will use. Additional requirements: they must carry their allocated competition number; use the power unit and tyres allocated to the nominated driver; and be in possession of a Super Licence or Free Practice Super Licence.

If one of the Competitor's nominated drivers is unable to drive after the end of initial scrutineering, and the stewards consent to a change, the replacement driver must use the Power Unit and tyres allocated to the original driver.

topic: Driving Rules
text:
The driver must drive the F1 Car alone and unaided. Drivers taking part in any session must always wear flame-resistant clothing, helmets, and Frontal Head Restraints (FHR) specified in the ISC Code. Drivers must observe the provisions of the ISC Code relating to driving behaviour on circuits at all times.

Official instructions will be given to drivers by means of the signals laid out in the ISC Code. Competitors must not use flags or lights similar to these. Light signals on trackside light panels have the same meaning as flag signals.

Single Waved Yellow Flag: Any driver passing through must reduce their speed and be prepared to change direction. To satisfy stewards, the driver is expected to have braked earlier and/or discernibly reduced speed in the relevant marshalling sector.

Double Waved Yellow Flag: Any driver passing through must reduce speed significantly and be prepared to change direction or stop. It must be clear that the driver has not attempted to set a meaningful lap time on the relevant lap. During sprint qualifying or qualifying, any driver passing through a double waved yellow flag marshalling sector will have that lap time deleted.

Double Waved Yellow Flag during Safety Car or VSC Period: The driver must also stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU in each marshalling sector concerned.

At no time may an F1 Car be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically, or in a manner which could be deemed potentially dangerous to other drivers or any other person. Drivers must make every reasonable effort to use the track at all times and may not leave the track without a justifiable reason. Drivers will be judged to have left the track if no part of the F1 Car remains in contact with it. White lines defining the track edges are considered to be part of the track but the kerbs are not. Should an F1 Car leave the track the driver may re-join, but only when it is safe to do so and without gaining any lasting advantage.

topic: Driving — Damaged Cars and Abandoned Cars
text:
Any driver whose car has significant and obvious damage to a structural component which results in an immediate risk of endangering the driver or others, or whose car has a significant failure or fault which means it cannot reasonably return to the Pit Lane without unnecessarily impeding another competitor or otherwise hindering the Competition must leave the track as soon as it is safe to do so. At the sole discretion of the Race Director, should a car be deemed to have such significant and obvious damage to a structural component, or such significant failure or fault, the Competitor may be instructed that the car must leave the track as soon as it is safe to do so.

A driver who abandons an F1 Car must leave it in neutral or with the clutch disengaged, with the ERS shut down and with the steering wheel in place.

Except during the suspension of a TTCS, any F1 Car abandoned on the circuit by its driver, even temporarily, shall be considered as withdrawn from the session. In exceptional circumstances, F1 Cars abandoned on the circuit during the suspension of a TTCS may be allowed to participate when that session resumes, provided they were not abandoned because of a mechanical issue, F1 Car damage, or in order to gain an advantage.

topic: Incidents — Reporting and Investigation
text:
The Race Director may report any on-track incident or suspected breach of the Sporting FIA F1 Regulations or the ISC Code (an "Incident") to the stewards.

It shall be at the discretion of the stewards to decide whether or not to proceed with an investigation. The stewards may also investigate an Incident noted by themselves. If an Incident is under investigation, a message informing all Competitors which driver or drivers are involved will be sent. Provided that such a message is displayed no later than sixty (60) minutes after the end-of-session signal of a TTCS has finished, the driver or drivers concerned may not leave the circuit without the consent of the stewards.

It shall be at the discretion of the stewards to decide if any driver involved in an Incident should be penalised. Unless it is clear to the stewards that a driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for an Incident, no penalty will be imposed. The stewards may impose the penalties specifically set out in the Sporting FIA F1 Regulations in addition to or instead of any other penalties available to them under the ISC Code.

topic: Penalties — LTCS
text:
In the event of an incident during any Lap Time Classified Session (LTCS — free practice, sprint qualifying, qualifying), the Stewards may delete a driver's lap time(s) or drop the driver such number of grid positions as they consider appropriate.

Unless it is completely clear that a driver committed a driving infringement, any such incident will normally be investigated after the relevant session.

Any such grid position penalties will be served in the Race, unless the driving infringement occurred in Sprint Qualifying, in which case the penalty will be applied to the grid of the Sprint.

topic: Penalties — TTCS Types
text:
In the event of an incident during any Total Time Classified Session (TTCS — sprint session or Race), the stewards may impose any one of the following penalties on any driver involved in an Incident:

(a) 5-Second Penalty: The driver must enter the Pit Lane, stop in their pit stop position for at least five seconds, then re-join the TTCS.

(b) 10-Second Penalty: The driver must enter the Pit Lane, stop in their pit stop position for at least ten seconds, then re-join the TTCS.

(c) Drive-Through Penalty: The driver must enter the Pit Lane and re-join the TTCS without stopping.

(d) Stop-and-Go Penalty (ten second stop-and-go time penalty): The driver must enter the Pit Lane, stop in their pit stop position for at least ten seconds, then re-join the TTCS.

(e) A time penalty.

(f) A Driver reprimand. Any driver who receives five (5) reprimands, at least four (4) of which are imposed for a driving infringement, in the same Championship, will upon the imposition of the fifth be given a ten (10) grid place penalty for the Race at that Competition. If the fifth reprimand is imposed following an Incident during a Race, the ten (10) grid place penalty will be applied for the Race at the driver's next Competition.

(g) A Competitor (F1 Team) reprimand.

(h) A drop of any number of grid positions for the next Sprint or Race in which the driver participates in the subsequent twelve (12) month period.

(i) Disqualification from the results.

(j) Suspension from the driver's next Competition.

topic: Penalties — Serving Procedures (5-Second and 10-Second)
text:
Should the stewards impose a 5-Second Penalty or 10-Second Penalty: the stewards will give written notification to the Competitor concerned and inform all Competitors using the OMS.

The driver must carry out the penalty the next time they enter the Pit Lane (except for entering the Pit Lane solely for the purpose of following the Safety Car per Article B5.13.3). For the avoidance of doubt, the driver must carry out the penalty if they elect to stop in their Designated Garage Area whilst a VSC or Safety Car procedure is in use, including when following the Safety Car through the Pit Lane.

The relevant driver may elect not to serve the penalty during the TTCS provided they carry out no further pit stop before the end of the TTCS. In such cases five (5) seconds will be added to the elapsed time of the driver in the case of a 5-Second Penalty, or ten (10) seconds in the case of a 10-Second Penalty.

Whilst an F1 Car is stationary in the Pit Lane as a result of incurring a 5-Second Penalty or 10-Second Penalty, it may not be worked on until the F1 Car has been stationary for the duration of the penalty. In this context, touching the F1 Car or driver by hand or tools or equipment will all constitute working.

topic: Penalties — Serving Procedures (Drive-Through and Stop-and-Go)
text:
For a Drive-Through Penalty or Stop-and-Go Penalty: From the time the Competitor is notified of the stewards' decision, the relevant driver may cross the Line on the track no more than twice before entering the Pit Lane.

Unless the driver was already in the Pit Entry Road or Pit Lane for the purpose of serving their penalty, they may not carry out the penalty if the VSC procedure is in use or after the Safety Car has been deployed. The number of times the driver crosses the Line behind the Safety Car or during the VSC procedure will be added to the maximum number of times they may cross the Line.

If either of these two penalties are imposed during the last three (3) laps, the relevant driver may cross the Line three times, and twenty (20) seconds will be added to the elapsed time in the case of a Drive-Through Penalty, or thirty (30) seconds in the case of a Stop-and-Go Penalty.

Whilst an F1 Car is stationary in the Pit Lane as a result of a Stop-and-Go Penalty it may not be worked on. However, if the engine stops and the driver is unable to restart it unaided, any work necessary to re-start it may be carried out after the time penalty period has elapsed. If the Competitor is unable to start the engine, the F1 Car may then only be worked on in the driver's garage.

If any of these four (4) penalties are imposed after the end of a TTCS: five (5) seconds for 5-Second Penalty, ten (10) seconds for 10-Second Penalty, twenty (20) seconds for Drive-Through Penalty, thirty (30) seconds for Stop-and-Go Penalty.

If any driver is unable to serve the penalty due to being unclassified (for 5-Second or 10-Second) or retiring from the TTCS (for Drive-Through or Stop-and-Go), the stewards may impose a grid place penalty at their next Race.

Any breach or failure to comply with the penalty serving procedures may result in a further penalty, which will supersede and replace the original penalty.

topic: Penalties — Appeals
text:
Pursuant to Articles A7.5.1 and A7.5.6, appeals may not be made against a decision concerning the following:

(a) Penalties imposed under Articles B1.9.5 a. to h., including those imposed during the last three (3) laps or after the end of a TTCS.
(b) Any drop of grid positions imposed under Article B8.2.
(c) Any penalty imposed under Article B1.9.4 (LTCS penalties).
(d) Any decision taken by the stewards in relation to Article B2.3.4 (Sprint grid) or B2.5.4 (Race grid).
(e) Any penalty imposed under Articles B5.5.3 or B5.15.2b.
(f) Any decision taken by the stewards under Article A3.3.1b.

topic: Competition Format — Free Practice Sessions
text:
Standard Format Competition (SFC — no sprint): Two (2) free practice sessions (FP1 and FP2), each lasting one (1) hour and separated by no less than two (2) hours and no more than three (3) hours, take place on the first day of on track running. If additional specifications of tyres are provided for ICTT (or if this has been scheduled and subsequently postponed or cancelled), FP2 will be increased in duration to one and a half (1.5) hours. A further free practice session (FP3), lasting one (1) hour and starting no less than eighteen (18) hours after the end of FP2, will take place on the second day of on track running. If additional tyres are provided for ICTT, FP3 will start no less than seventeen and a half (17.5) hours after the end of FP2.

Alternative Format Competition (AFC — with sprint): One (1) free practice session (FP1), lasting one (1) hour, will take place on the first day of on track running.

Free Practice Session Classification: The classification of all free practice sessions shall be determined based upon fastest lap time set by each driver during the session, with the driver with the fastest lap time in first position, and so on.

topic: Competition Format — Sprint Qualifying Session
text:
At each Alternative Format Competition, the starting grid of the Sprint will be determined by the results of the sprint qualifying session (Sprint Qualifying or SQ), which will take place on the first day of track running and start no less than two and a half (2.5) hours, and no more than three and a half (3.5) hours after the end of FP1.

Sprint Qualifying Format: SQ1 runs for twelve (12) minutes — all F1 Cars permitted, and at the end, the slowest six (6) F1 Cars are eliminated. Lap times of the remaining sixteen (16) F1 Cars are then deleted. After a seven (7) minute break, SQ2 runs for ten (10) minutes — remaining sixteen (16) F1 Cars permitted, and at the end, the slowest six (6) F1 Cars are eliminated. Lap times of the remaining ten (10) F1 Cars are then deleted. After a seven (7) minute break, SQ3 runs for eight (8) minutes — remaining ten (10) F1 Cars permitted on the track.

Sprint Qualifying Classification: Top ten (10) positions allocated to SQ3 drivers by fastest lap time. Next six (6) positions to SQ2 eliminated drivers by fastest lap time (11th position for fastest). Next six (6) positions to SQ1 eliminated drivers by fastest lap time (17th position for fastest). If two or more drivers set identical lap times, priority given to the one who set it first. If more than one driver fails to set a lap time during SQ2 or SQ3, they are arranged by: (A) any driver who attempted to set a lap time by starting a flying lap; (B) any driver who failed to start a flying lap; (C) any driver who failed to leave the pits during the period; with relative classification determined by previous period classification.

Drivers will be considered "unclassified" if: (i) eliminated in SQ1 and best lap exceeded 107% of fastest SQ1 lap (unless track declared wet); (ii) failed to set a lap time in SQ1, or all lap times were deleted; (iii) got disqualified by the Stewards from Sprint Qualifying. The procedures are based upon twenty-two (22) F1 Cars being eligible. If twenty (20) F1 Cars are eligible, five (5) F1 Cars will be eliminated after SQ1 and SQ2. If twenty-four (24) F1 Cars are eligible, seven (7) F1 Cars will be eliminated after SQ1 and SQ2.

topic: Competition Format — Sprint Session
text:
At each Alternative Format Competition, a sprint session (Sprint or SP) will take place on the second day of track running.

Sprint Session Distance: The distance of each Sprint, from the start signal to the end-of-session signal, shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 100km. If the formation lap(s) is started behind the Safety Car, the number of Sprint laps will be reduced by the number of laps carried out by the Safety Car minus one.

Sprint Session Duration: Should one (1) hour elapse from the start signal before the scheduled Sprint distance is completed, the leader will be shown the end-of-session signal when they cross the Line at the end of the lap following the lap during which the one (1) hour period ended, provided this does not result in the scheduled number of laps being exceeded. Should the Sprint be suspended, the duration of the suspension will be added to this one (1) hour period up to a maximum total Sprint duration of one and a half (1.5) hours. If the formation lap for the Sprint is started behind the Safety Car, the maximum total Sprint duration of one and a half (1.5) hours will commence at the time the green lights on the start gantry are illuminated.

Sprint Session Classification: The F1 Car placed first will be the one having covered the scheduled distance in the shortest time. All F1 Cars will be classified taking into account the number of complete laps they have covered. F1 Cars having covered less than 90% of the number of laps covered by the winner (rounded down to the nearest whole number) will not be classified.

topic: Competition Format — Sprint Grid Formation
text:
The grid for the Sprint will be formed in accordance with the results of Sprint Qualifying and the Sprint Qualifying classification process. Any penalties received for the Sprint will be added up and applied using the procedure defined in this article.

If Sprint Qualifying does not take place at a Competition (accepted by Stewards that the session cannot take place), the grid for the Sprint will be defined based upon the Drivers' Championship classification. If neither method can be applied, the formation of the grid shall be at the sole discretion of the Stewards.

Starting from a nominally empty grid, drivers will be allocated their grid positions in the following sequence: (i) Classified drivers who have received 15 or less cumulative unserved grid penalties for the Sprint imposed in the previous twelve (12) months will be allocated a temporary grid position equal to their Sprint Qualifying classification plus the sum of their unserved grid penalties. If two or more drivers share a temporary grid position, their relative order will be determined in accordance with Sprint Qualifying classification, with the slowest driver keeping their allocated position, and the other drivers getting temporary positions immediately ahead of them. (ii) Following allocation of temporary grid positions to penalised drivers, unpenalised classified drivers will be allocated any unoccupied grid position in the sequence of their Sprint Qualifying session classification. (iii) Following allocation to unpenalised classified drivers, penalised drivers with a temporary grid position will be moved up to fill any unoccupied grid position. (iv) Classified drivers who have accrued more than 15 cumulative unserved grid position penalties for the Sprint imposed in the previous twelve (12) months will start behind any other classified driver; relative position determined in accordance with Sprint Qualifying session classification. (v) Unclassified drivers permitted to participate will be allocated grid positions behind all classified drivers.

The provisional starting grid will be published no less than two (2) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Sprint. Competitors whose F1 Car is unable to start must inform the stewards no later than one and a quarter (1¼) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap of the Sprint. The final starting grid will be published one (1) hour before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Sprint.

topic: Competition Format — Qualifying Session
text:
The starting grid of the Race will be determined by the results of the Race qualifying session (Qualifying or Q), which will take place: (a) At each Standard Format Competition on the second day of on track running, starting no less than two (2) hours, and no more than three (3) hours after the end of FP3; (b) At each Alternative Format Competition on the second day of track running, starting no less than three (3) hours, and no more than four (4) hours after the end of the Sprint.

Qualifying Format: Q1 runs for eighteen (18) minutes — all F1 Cars permitted, and at the end, the slowest six (6) F1 Cars are prohibited from taking any further part. Lap times of the remaining sixteen (16) F1 Cars are then deleted. After a seven (7) minute break, Q2 runs for fifteen (15) minutes — remaining sixteen (16) F1 Cars permitted, and at the end, the slowest six (6) F1 Cars are eliminated. Lap times of the remaining ten (10) F1 Cars are then deleted. After an eight (8) minute break, Q3 runs for twelve (12) minutes — remaining ten (10) F1 Cars permitted.

Qualifying Classification: Top ten (10) positions allocated to Q3 drivers by fastest lap time. Next six (6) positions to Q2 eliminated drivers (11th position for fastest). Next six (6) positions to Q1 eliminated drivers (17th position for fastest). If two or more drivers set identical times, priority given to the one who set it first. Drivers considered "unclassified" if: (i) best lap in Q1 exceeded 107% of fastest Q1 lap (unless track declared wet); (ii) failed to set a lap time in Q1, or all lap times were deleted; (iii) got disqualified from Qualifying. The procedures are based upon twenty-two (22) F1 Cars being eligible.

topic: Competition Format — Race Session
text:
The Race session (Race or R) will take place on the third day of track running at all Competitions.

Race Session Distance: The distance of the Race, from the start signal to the end-of-session signal, shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 305km. Exception: if the formation lap(s) is started behind the Safety Car, the number of Race laps will be reduced by the number of laps carried out by the Safety Car minus one. The distance of the Race in Monaco shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 260km.

Race Session Duration: Should two hours elapse from the start signal before the scheduled Race distance is completed, the leader will be shown the end-of-session signal when they cross the Line at the end of the lap following the lap during which the two (2) hour period ended, provided this does not result in the scheduled number of laps being exceeded. Should the Race be suspended, the duration of the suspension will be added to this two (2) hour period up to a maximum total Race duration of three (3) hours.

Race Classification: The F1 Car placed first will be the one having covered the scheduled distance in the shortest time. All F1 Cars classified taking into account the number of complete laps they have covered. F1 Cars having covered less than 90% of the number of laps covered by the winner (rounded down to the nearest whole number) will not be classified.

topic: Competition Format — Race Grid Formation
text:
The grid for the Race will be formed in accordance with the results of Qualifying, the Qualifying classification process, and the procedure defined in this article. If Qualifying does not take place (accepted by Stewards), the grid will be defined based upon the Drivers' Championship classification. If neither method can be applied, the formation shall be at the sole discretion of the Stewards.

Starting from a nominally empty grid, drivers will be allocated their grid positions in the following sequence: (i) Classified drivers who have received 15 or less cumulative unserved grid penalties for the Race imposed in the previous twelve (12) months will be allocated a temporary grid position equal to their Qualifying classification plus the sum of their unserved grid penalties. If two or more drivers share a temporary grid position, their relative order will be determined in accordance with their Qualifying session classification, with the slowest driver keeping their allocated temporary grid position, and the other drivers getting temporary grid positions immediately ahead of them. (ii) Following allocation of temporary grid positions to penalised drivers, unpenalised classified drivers will be allocated any unoccupied grid position in the sequence of their Qualifying session or sprint qualifying session classification. (iii) Following allocation to unpenalised classified drivers, penalised drivers with a temporary grid position will be moved up to fill any unoccupied grid position. (iv) Classified drivers who have accrued more than 15 cumulative unserved grid position penalties for the Race imposed in the previous twelve (12) months will start behind any other classified driver. (v) Unclassified drivers permitted to participate will be allocated grid positions behind all classified drivers.

The provisional starting grid will be published no less than two (2) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Race. Competitors whose F1 Car is unable to start must inform the stewards no later than one and a quarter (1¼) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap of the Race. The final starting grid will be published one (1) hour before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Race.

topic: Scrutineering Procedures
text:
Each Competitor will be required to carry out initial scrutineering of their F1 Cars, which will commence four (4) hours prior to the start of FP1 and, unless prior written permission has been granted by the Technical Delegate, submit the duly completed declaration no later than two (2) hours before the start of FP1. No F1 Car may take part in the Competition until the declaration has been submitted and the Technical Delegate has confirmed they are satisfied it has been fully and correctly completed.

Any Competitor whose F1 Car has a change of survival cell after initial scrutineering must complete a new declaration for approval by the Technical Delegate. At each Standard Format Competition, any such F1 Car scrutineered after the start of FP1 may not be used until the start of FP3; any such F1 Car scrutineered after the start of FP3 may not be used until the pit exit is opened before the Race. At each Alternative Format Competition, any such F1 Car scrutineered after the start of FP1 may not be used until the pit exit is opened before the Sprint.

The scrutineers may: (a) Check the eligibility of an F1 Car or Competitor at any time during a Competition; (b) Require an F1 Car to be dismantled to make sure conditions of eligibility or conformity are fully satisfied; (c) Require a Competitor to pay reasonable expenses; (d) Require a Competitor to supply parts or samples at a location determined by the FIA (Competitor is responsible for adequate packaging, shipping including insurance; packaging must allow FIA anti-tamper features or seals to be applied; the FIA and Competitor will agree a delivery schedule; packaging, anti-tamper features, and delivery schedule must be approved in writing by the Technical Delegate prior to shipment).

The Race Director may require that any F1 Car involved in an accident be stopped and checked. The stewards will publish the findings of the scrutineers each time F1 Cars are checked. These results will not include any specific figure except when an F1 Car is found to be in breach of the Technical FIA F1 Regulations. From twenty-four (24) hours prior to the start of the Competition, it is the sole responsibility of the Competitor to provide without delay, upon request of the Technical Delegate, any F1 Team specific items such as adaptors, fixtures, lifting devices, tools, wiring looms or connectors required to facilitate the undertaking of scrutineering checks.

topic: Weighing Procedures
text:
After any LTCS, during Sprint Qualifying, or during Qualifying, F1 Cars will be weighed as follows: (a) When signalled to do so the driver will proceed directly to the FIA garage and stop their engine; (b) Any driver who fails to stop when asked to do so and then fails to bring the F1 Car back to the FIA garage, or if work is carried out on the F1 Car before it is returned to the FIA garage, will be referred to the stewards; (c) Each driver must be weighed by the Technical Delegate at the end of the last period of the Qualifying or Sprint Qualifying session in which they participated; (d) At the end of Qualifying or Sprint Qualifying all F1 Cars which took part in Q3 (or SQ3) will be weighed; if a driver wishes to leave their F1 Car before it is weighed, they must ask the Technical Delegate to weigh them in order that this weight may be added to that of the F1 Car; (e) If an F1 Car stops on the circuit during Qualifying or Sprint Qualifying and the driver leaves the F1 Car, they must go to the FIA garage immediately on their return to the Pit Lane.

After any TTCS any classified F1 Car may be weighed. If a Driver wishes to leave their F1 Car before it is weighed, they must present themselves to the Technical Delegate and request to be weighed separately.

The relevant F1 Car may be disqualified should its weight be less than that specified in Article C4.1 when weighed, save where the deficiency in weight results from the accidental loss of a component.

No substance may be added to, placed on, or removed from an F1 Car after it has been selected for weighing or has finished any TTCS, or during the weighing procedure (except by a scrutineer when acting in their official capacity). In the event of any breach of these provisions, the stewards may drop the driver such number of grid positions as they consider appropriate or disqualify them from the TTCS.

topic: Covering of Components
text:
Commencing twenty-nine (29) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1, no screen, cover, or other obstruction which in any way obscures any part of an F1 Car will be allowed at any time in the paddock, garages, Pit Lane, or grid, unless it is clear any such covers are needed solely for mechanical reasons (such as protecting against fire).

The following are specifically NOT permitted: Engine, gearbox, or radiator covers whilst engines are being changed or moved around the garage; covers over spare wings when they are on a stand in the Pit Lane not being used; parts such as spare floors, fuel rigs, or tool trolleys may not be used as an obstruction.

The following ARE permitted: Covers over damaged F1 Cars or components; a transparent tool tray no more than 50mm deep placed on top of the rear wing; warming or heat retaining covers for the engine and gearbox on the grid; a rear wing cover designed specifically to protect a mechanic starting the F1 Car from fire; covers over the tyre manufacturer's code numbers (not FIA bar code numbers); a cover over the F1 Car in the parc fermé overnight; a cover over the F1 Car in the Pit Lane or grid if it is raining; tyre heating blankets as described in the Technical Regulations.

topic: Sealing of Cars — Standard Format Competition
text:
At each Standard Format Competition: Within three (3) hours of the end of FP2, all F1 Cars used during the session (or which were intended for use but failed to leave the Pit Lane) must be covered and ready for FIA seals to be applied (with the exception of when a Competitor is using one of their permitted exceptions to Restricted Period 3). For this article only, an F1 Car is defined as all components required to comply with the Technical Regulations with the exception of the Floor Bodywork, the Nose Bodywork, the Front Wing Bodywork, and the Rear Wing Bodywork. Components must be of a specification already used at the Competition or intended as an option. Obsolete or dummy components are not permitted. If the F1 Car is supported on stands, all F1 Car components must be present under the cover. The complete F1 Car (minus any exceptions and including any non-fitted components) must remain in view of the overhead camera at all times. Permitted breather, heating, or cooling devices may be fitted. Failure to comply with this requirement will be equivalent to a breach of Restricted Period 3, and failure to comply with both Articles will be considered as a single breach.

Three (3) hours before the start of FP3, the FIA seals and covers may be removed.

topic: Sealing of Cars — Alternative Format and All Competitions
text:
At each Alternative Format Competition: Within two (2) hours of the end of Sprint Qualifying, all F1 Cars used during the session (or which were intended for use but failed to leave the Pit Lane) must be covered and ready for FIA seals to be applied. For marketing purposes this deadline may be extended for one F1 Car from each Competitor for a maximum of two (2) hours by prior arrangement with the Technical Delegate. In the case of a breach, it will also be considered that the Competitor has breached Article B3.5.7 (parc fermé conditions), and the relevant driver will be penalised by a single penalty for the combination of both offences. Three (3) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the sprint, the seals and covers may be removed but the F1 Cars will remain under parc fermé conditions until the start of the sprint.

At each Competition (all formats): Within two (2) hours of the end of Qualifying, all F1 Cars used during the session (or which were intended for use but failed to leave the Pit Lane) must be covered and ready for FIA seals to be applied. The marketing extension rule applies as above. Five (5) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Race, the seals and covers may be removed but the F1 Cars will remain under parc fermé conditions until the start of the Race. Whilst F1 Cars are covered and sealed, they may be fitted with devices to keep them warm.

topic: Pre-Sprint and Pre-Race Parc Fermé
text:
Each F1 Car will be deemed to be in parc fermé from: (a) the time at which it leaves the Pit Lane for the first time during the Sprint Qualifying until the start of the Sprint; and (b) from the time at which it leaves the Pit Lane for the first time during Qualifying until the start of the Race. Any F1 Car which fails to leave the Pit Lane during the sprint qualifying session or qualifying session will be deemed to be in parc fermé at the end of SQ1 or Q1 respectively.

Each Competitor must provide the Technical Delegate with a suspension set-up sheet for both of their F1 Cars before each of them leaves the Pit Lane for the first time during the sprint qualifying session and the qualifying session.

When deemed to be in parc fermé, other than when the F1 Cars are sealed, only the work listed in Appendix B2 may be carried out. Any parts removed must remain close to the F1 Car and visible to the scrutineer assigned to the relevant F1 Car; any parts removed must be refitted before the F1 Car leaves the Pit Lane.

Any work not listed in Appendix B2 may only be undertaken with the approval of the Technical Delegate following a written request. It must be clear that any replacement part a Competitor wishes to fit is the same in design and similar in mass, inertia, and function to the original. Any parts removed shall be retained by the FIA.

If a Competitor wishes to change a part during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, on the grid before the start of the Sprint and between reconnaissance laps, and/or on the grid before the start of the Race, this may be done without first seeking the permission of the Technical Delegate, provided it is reasonable to believe permission would be given if there was time to ask and the broken or damaged part remains in full view of the scrutineer at all times.

Exceptionally, six (6) times during the Championship, requests for replacement parts of Front Wing Bodywork, Rear Wing Bodywork, Rear Bodywork, or Floor Bodywork that are different in design will be considered for approval, provided the replacement part is of a specification previously used in Pre-Season Public Collective Testing, a Sprint Qualifying session, a Qualifying session, or a TTCS.

A Competitor may not modify any part on the F1 Car or make changes to the set-up of the suspension whilst in parc fermé. In the case of a breach: At each Standard Format Competition, the relevant driver must start the Race from the Pit Lane. At each Alternative Format Competition, if the breach is before the start of the Sprint, the relevant driver must start the Sprint from the Pit Lane; if after the start of Qualifying, the relevant driver must start the Race from the Pit Lane.

One (1) scrutineer will be allocated to each F1 Car for the purpose of ensuring that no unauthorised work is carried out whilst F1 Cars are being held under parc fermé conditions. A list of parts replaced with the specific agreement of the Technical Delegate will be published and distributed to all Competitors prior to the Race.

topic: Post Sprint and Post Race Parc Fermé
text:
Only those officials charged with supervision may enter the parc fermé. No intervention of any kind is allowed there unless authorised by such officials. When the parc fermé is in use, parc fermé regulations will apply in the area between the Line and the parc fermé entrance.

The parc fermé shall be secured such that no unauthorised persons can gain access to it. A maximum of three (3) team personnel per F1 Car will be permitted access to the Parc Fermé area for the sole purpose of fitting cooling fans and undertaking any work required by those officials charged with supervision of parc fermé.

Each Driver must remain fully attired until after they have been weighed (e.g.: Helmet, Gloves, etc.). Drivers must not interfere with parc fermé protocols in any way.

topic: Lap Time Classified Sessions (LTCS) — General Provisions
text:
Any driver taking part in any LTCS who, in the opinion of the stewards, stops unnecessarily on the circuit or unnecessarily impedes another driver shall be subject to the penalties referred to in Article B1.9.4.

Should it become necessary to stop any LTCS, the Race Director will order red flags to be shown at all marshal posts and the orange lights on the start gantry to be illuminated at the Line. When the signal is given to stop, all F1 Cars must immediately reduce speed and proceed slowly back to the Pit Lane. In order to ensure that drivers reduce speed sufficiently, from the time at which the "RED FLAG" message is sent until the time that each F1 Car crosses the first safety car line when entering the Pit Lane, drivers must stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU at least once in each marshalling sector.

At the end of each LTCS, any period of Qualifying (Q1, Q2, Q3), or any period of Sprint Qualifying (SQ1, SQ2, SQ3), no driver may cross the Line more than once. The Race Director may interrupt a LTCS as often and for as long as they deem necessary to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the Competition.

The VSC procedure may be initiated to neutralise a LTCS on the order of the Race Director. When deployed, a message "VSC DEPLOYED" will be sent to all Competitors and all FIA light panels will display "VSC". During VSC: No F1 Car may be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically, or in a potentially dangerous manner. All competing F1 Cars must reduce speed and stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU at least once in each marshalling sector and at both the first and second safety car lines; all F1 Cars must also be above this minimum time when FIA light panels change to green. No driver may overtake another F1 Car except: when entering pits (after reaching first safety car line); when leaving pits (before reaching second safety car line); whilst in Pit Entry Road, Pit Lane, or Pit Exit Road; or if any F1 Car slows with an obvious problem. When the Race Director decides it is safe to end the VSC procedure, "VSC ENDING" will be sent and, at any time between 10 and 15 seconds later, "VSC" on the FIA light panels will change to green. After 30 seconds the green lights will be extinguished.

topic: LTCS — Free Practice and Qualifying Specific Provisions
text:
Free Practice: Subject to the provisions of Article B2.2.1, if Free Practice 1 at an Alternative Format Competition is interrupted before forty-five (45) minutes of the session has elapsed, this session may be extended such that the time cars are permitted on track during this session is maintained in accordance with Article B2.1.2.

Practice Starts on the Grid: After the end of each free practice session, any driver on track when the end-of-session signal is shown may carry out a practice start on the grid. Any such driver wishing to perform a practice start must: (a) Cross the Line following the end-of-session signal being shown, complete one (1) further lap and proceed to the grid; (b) Perform the start from a marked grid position, pulling as far forward on the grid as possible; (c) Under no circumstances perform a practice start if another F1 Car remains stationary in front of them on the same side of the grid. If the Race Director considers it necessary to stop practice starts, a red flag will be displayed, and the orange lights on the start gantry will be illuminated.

Sprint Qualifying and Qualifying Sessions: If any period is interrupted, the interrupted period will be extended such that the time cars are permitted on track during that period is maintained. If any period is interrupted at a point when the Race Director determines that no F1 Car could subsequently leave the Pit Lane and start a timed lap prior to the end of that period, at the sole discretion of the Race Director the interrupted period may not be resumed, i.e. that part of the Competition will be stopped. Any driver whose F1 Car stops in any area other than the Pit Lane during Sprint Qualifying or Qualifying and receives physical assistance will not be permitted to take any further part in that session.

topic: Total Time Classified Sessions (TTCS) — General Provisions
text:
No driver may start a TTCS without taking part in at least one (1) LTCS. The layout of the Grid will be in a staggered 1 x 1 formation and the rows on the Grid will be separated by 16 metres.

All equipment used to cool the F1 Car on the Grid using forced air flow (or any other gaseous flow) must only be powered by electricity.

Fuel may not be added to nor removed from an F1 Car after it has left the Pit Lane to start the reconnaissance lap(s) until the end-of-session signal has been shown.

Other than where permitted during the suspension of a TTCS, tyre blankets are not permitted in the Pit Lane at any time during a TTCS and must be removed before the tyres are carried to the pit stop area.

Except for the circumstances described in Article B1.5.4d or Article B5.14, any driver whose F1 Car stops in any area other than the Pit Lane during a TTCS and receives physical assistance resulting in the F1 Car re-joining may be disqualified from that TTCS.

The FIA Safety Car will be driven by an FIA appointed Safety Car driver and will carry an FIA Safety Car observer capable of recognising all the competing F1 Cars who is in permanent radio contact with Race control.

Unless specifically authorised by the Race Director, during the start of any TTCS the pit wall must be kept free of all persons with the exception of team personnel permitted under Article B1.5.8, officials, and fire marshals.

The mass of oil contained in each oil tank, with the exception of the main oil tank, must be declared to the FIA one (1) hour before the scheduled start of any TTCS.

topic: TTCS — Reconnaissance Laps
text:
Prior to the Pit Lane opening for the reconnaissance lap(s), the Safety Car will leave the Pit Lane and take up position at the front of the grid, remaining there until the five (5) minute signal is given. At this point (except under Article B5.10) it will cover a lap of the track and take up position.

Prior to the scheduled start of the formation lap for each TTCS, the pit exit will be opened and all F1 Cars (including any required to start the TTCS from the Pit Lane) will be permitted to leave the Pit Lane to cover reconnaissance lap(s). All drivers going to the pit exit at this time must do so at a constant speed and with constant throttle, this applies over the whole of the Pit Lane.

For each Sprint: the pit exit will be opened thirty (30) minutes before the scheduled start of the formation lap and shall remain open for five (5) minutes. Each driver may complete one (1) reconnaissance lap.

For each Race: the pit exit will be opened forty (40) minutes before the scheduled start of the formation lap and shall remain open for ten (10) minutes. Should any driver wish to cover more than one (1) reconnaissance lap, this must be done by driving down the Pit Entry Road and Pit Lane at greatly reduced speed between each lap. If a driver stops in their Designated Garage Area between reconnaissance laps, the F1 Car may only re-join the track by being driven from the driver's garage and not from their pit stop position.

At the end of these laps, all F1 Cars starting the TTCS from the grid should stop on the grid in starting order with their engines stopped, and all F1 Cars required to start from the Pit Lane must enter the Pit Lane.

Any F1 Car which does not complete a reconnaissance lap and reach the grid under its own power will not be permitted to start the TTCS from the grid. Any F1 Car which is still in the Pit Lane when the pit exit is closed after the reconnaissance laps can start the TTCS from the end of the Pit Lane provided it got there under its own power.

topic: TTCS — Pit Lane Starters
text:
With the exception of the reconnaissance laps, any driver required to start the TTCS from the Pit Lane may not drive their F1 Car from their Competitors Designated Garage Area until the Pit Lane exit is closed before the scheduled start of the formation lap and must stop in a line in the Fast Lane.

If more than one F1 Car will start from the Pit Lane, they must line up in the order established under Article B2.3.4 (Sprint) or B2.5.4 (Race). However, any F1 Car reaching the end of the Pit Lane after the five (5) minute signal must start behind any F1 Car already at the pit exit.

Working in the Fast Lane will be permitted for a period ending fifteen (15) seconds prior to the commencement of the formation lap, after which all personnel and equipment must be clear of the Fast Lane. Any such work is restricted to: starting the engine and any directly associated preparation; the fitting or removal of permitted cooling and heating devices; changes made for driver comfort; subject to Article B5.5.3, changing wheels and tyres; in accordance with Article C3.10.10, adjustment of the position (not controlled by the FIA Standard ECU) of the Front Wing Profiles. No parts may be added, removed, or replaced. At all times drivers must follow the directions of the marshals.

topic: TTCS — Grid Procedure
text:
The approach of the start of a TTCS will be announced by signals shown ten (10) minutes, five (5) minutes, three (3) minutes, one (1) minute, and fifteen (15) seconds before the start of the formation lap, each accompanied by an audible warning.

Ten (10) minute signal: everybody except drivers, officials, and team technical staff must leave the grid. If track conditions are unsuitable, the formation lap(s) may take place behind the Safety Car; in that case the Safety Car's orange lights will be illuminated and all Competitors will be informed using the OMS. The use of wet-weather tyres is compulsory in such circumstance.

Five (5) minute signal: All F1 Cars on the grid and any F1 Cars in the Pit Lane Fast Lane must have their wheels fitted. After this signal, wheels may only be removed in the Inner Lane. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver whose F1 Car did not have all its wheels fully fitted at the five (5) minute signal. Tyre blankets on the wheels fitted must be disconnected from any power supply and must not be reconnected during the start procedure (unless the delayed start or aborted start signal is subsequently shown). F1 Team personnel and equipment trolleys must commence leaving the grid.

Three (3) minute signal: No more than sixteen (16) team personnel for each Competitor are permitted on the grid.

One (1) minute signal: Engines should be started and all team personnel must leave the grid (and the pit lane Fast Lane if working per B5.3.3) by the time the fifteen (15) second signal is given, taking all equipment with them. If any team personnel are touching an F1 Car or team equipment is connected to an F1 Car on the grid after the fifteen (15) second signal has been shown, the driver concerned must start the TTCS from the Pit Lane (Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to start from the Pit Lane). If any team personnel are touching a car or team equipment is connected to a car in the pit lane Fast Lane after the fifteen (15) second signal, a Drive-Through Penalty will be imposed on that driver. If any driver needs assistance after the fifteen (15) second signal they must immediately raise their hands above their head; when the remainder of the F1 Cars able to do so have left the grid, marshals will be instructed to push the F1 Car into the Pit Lane Inner Lane.

topic: TTCS — Formation Lap
text:
When the green lights on the start gantry are illuminated, all F1 Cars on the grid able to do so should leave the grid and begin the formation lap with the pole position driver leading.

Once all cars on track have passed the end of the Pit Lane on the formation lap, the pit exit will be opened and all cars starting from the Pit Lane able to do so must leave the Pit Lane and join the formation lap. When such cars are permitted to leave the Pit Lane they must do so in the order that was established under B5.3.2 unless another car is unduly delayed. Once all such cars have left the Pit Lane the pit exit will be closed. All such cars must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the formation lap.

When leaving the grid all drivers must respect the Pit Lane speed limit until they pass pole position. During the formation lap practice starts are forbidden and the formation must be kept as tight as possible.

Overtaking during the formation lap is only permitted if an F1 Car is delayed and F1 Cars behind cannot avoid passing it without unduly delaying the remainder of the field. In this case, drivers may only overtake to re-establish the original starting order. Any driver delayed in this way, and who is unable to re-establish the original starting order before they reach the first safety F1 Car line, must enter the Pit Lane and start the TTCS from the end of the Pit Lane. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to enter the Pit Lane if they have not re-established the original starting order before they reach the first safety F1 Car line.

topic: TTCS — Start Procedure
text:
At any time after the formation lap has commenced and prior to the start of the TTCS, if an F1 Car is immobilised on the starting grid: (i) The driver must immediately raise their hands above their head; (ii) The marshals alongside the grid must immediately wave yellow flags and/or activate the yellow grid light panel; (iii) When the Race Director deems it safe, it shall be the duty of the marshals to push any immobilised F1 Car into the Pit Lane Inner Lane by the fastest route. Any driver being pushed from the grid may not attempt to start the F1 Car. (iv) Once the F1 Car is in the Pit Lane Inner Lane, the Competitor may then attempt to start the F1 Car; if successful the F1 Car may only enter the Fast Lane once the TTCS has started.

When the F1 Cars starting from the grid return to the grid at the end of the formation lap, they must stop within their respective starting grid positions, keeping their engines running. There will be a standing start, the signal to start the TTCS being given by means of five red lights on the start gantry, operated by the permanent starter. Once all F1 Cars have come to a halt, the first red light will be illuminated followed sequentially by the second, third, fourth, and fifth red lights. At any time after the fifth red light is illuminated, the signal to start will be given by extinguishing all red lights. The time interval between the illumination of each of the five red lights shall be one (1) second. The time interval between the illumination of the fifth light and all lights being extinguished is at the sole discretion of the permanent starter.

When the cars required to start from the Pit Lane return to the Pit Lane at the end of the formation lap, they must proceed to pit exit at a constant speed and with constant throttle and stop in a line in the Fast Lane in the order in which they arrive, keeping their engines running. Once all cars on track have passed the end of the Pit Lane for the first time after the start, the pit exit will be opened and all cars starting from the Pit Lane may then join the TTCS.

topic: TTCS — Aborted Start and Extra Formation Lap
text:
Aborted Start: If at any time after the formation lap has commenced and prior to the start of the TTCS a problem arises that could endanger the start, the Race Director may decide the start should be aborted. Procedures: (a) once all cars able to do so have completed the formation lap and returned to their allocated position on the grid, the orange lights on the start gantry will be illuminated, a board saying "ABORTED START" will be displayed, and the message "ABORTED START" will be sent to all Competitors; (b) All cars starting from the grid should remain in their allocated position; all cars starting from the Pit Lane should remain in their position in the Fast Lane; F1 Team personnel and equipment trolleys will be permitted access to the grid; (c) When a new start time is known, all Competitors will be informed; the starting procedure will begin again at the ten (10) minute signal. Any driver who caused an aborted start and is then subsequently able to start the TTCS must start from the end of the Pit Lane; if more than one car is involved, their starting order will be determined by the order in which they reached the end of the Pit Lane. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to start from the Pit Lane. For each Aborted Start procedure completed, the TTCS will be shortened by one (1) lap.

Extra Formation Lap: If a problem arises that could endanger the start but does not necessitate an aborted start, the Race Director may decide an extra formation lap is required. Procedures: (a) Orange lights on the start gantry will be illuminated, a board saying "EXTRA FORMATION LAP" will be displayed, and after two (2) seconds the green lights will be illuminated, signalling all cars to complete an extra formation lap; (b) When leaving the grid to complete the extra formation lap all drivers must respect the Pit Lane speed limit until they pass pole position; (c) Any cars that were starting from the Pit Lane must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the formation lap, proceed to pit exit, and join the Extra Formation Lap once all cars on track have passed the end of the Pit Lane for the first time. Any driver who caused an extra formation lap and is then able to start any extra formation lap must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the lap and start the TTCS from the end of the Pit Lane. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to start from the Pit Lane. For each Extra Formation Lap procedure completed, the TTCS will be shortened by one (1) lap. Should Article B5.9 apply, the TTCS will nevertheless count for the Championship no matter how often the procedure is repeated.

topic: TTCS — Formation Laps Behind Safety Car
text:
If track conditions are considered unsuitable to start the TTCS at the scheduled time, formation lap(s) may take place behind the Safety Car. If the Race Director deems it necessary to mandate wet-weather tyres, at the ten (10) minute signal the Safety Car orange lights will be illuminated and the message "FORMATION LAP(S) BEHIND SAFETY CAR - WET WEATHER TYRES MUST BE USED" will be sent; the use of wet-weather tyres is compulsory. If the Race Director does not deem it necessary to mandate wet-weather tyres, at the five (5) minute signal the Safety Car orange lights will be illuminated and the message "FORMATION LAP(S) BEHIND SAFETY CAR" will be sent.

When the green lights on the start gantry are illuminated, the Safety Car will leave the grid and all drivers must follow in grid order no more than the maximum allowable gap of ten (10) car lengths apart. At the sole discretion of the Race Director, the maximum allowable gap may be increased to twenty (20) car lengths in poor visibility conditions — the message "LOW VISIBILITY – MAXIMUM GAP TWENTY CAR LENGTHS" will be sent. The Safety Car will continue until conditions are considered suitable for competition.

Any F1 Cars starting from the Pit Lane must join the formation lap(s) once all cars on track have passed the end of the Pit Lane for the first time. Any such F1 Cars must complete all formation laps and must enter the Pit Lane after the Safety Car returns to the pits and start the TTCS from the end of the Pit Lane in the order they get there.

If the formation lap(s) is started behind the Safety Car, the TTCS will be shortened by the number of laps carried out by the Safety Car minus one.

Standing Start: If after the formation laps behind the Safety Car have commenced, the track conditions are considered suitable to start the TTCS from a standing start, the message "STANDING START" will be sent, all FIA light panels will display "SS", the Pit Lane exit will be closed, and the Safety Car orange lights will be extinguished. Once the Safety Car has entered the Pit Lane, all F1 Cars (except those required to start from the Pit Lane) can return to the grid, take up their grid positions, and follow the procedures set out in Article B5.7.

Rolling Start: If track conditions are considered unsuitable for a standing start, the message "ROLLING START" will be sent, FIA light panels will display "RS", the Pit Lane exit will be closed, and the Safety Car orange lights will be extinguished. As the Safety Car is approaching the Pit Entry Road, the FIA light panels will be extinguished and a green flag and/or green light panel will be displayed at the Line. No driver may overtake another F1 Car on the track until they pass the Line for the first time after the Safety Car has returned to the pits. The TTCS will be deemed to have started when the leading F1 Car crosses the Line after the Safety Car has returned to the pits.

topic: TTCS — False Start
text:
During any standing start (Articles B5.7.2 or B5.10.8) or standing start resumption (Article B5.15.4), all cars must be:

(a) Stationary in their allocated grid position for the period after the third red light is illuminated and before the start signal is given by extinguishing all red lights, as defined in Article B5.7.1b; or

(b) Positioned in their allocated grid position on the starting grid in such a way that the transponder is unable to detect the moment at which the F1 Car first moved from its grid position after the start signal is given; or

(c) Positioned in their allocated grid position such that no part of the contact patch of their front tyres are outside of the lines (front and sides) at the time of the start signal.

At the sole discretion of the stewards, a 5-Second Penalty, a 10-Second Penalty, a Drive-Through Penalty, or a Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who is judged to have breached this article.

topic: TTCS — Virtual Safety Car (VSC)
text:
The Virtual Safety Car will be used when double waved yellow flags are needed on any section of track and Competitors or officials may be in danger, but the circumstances are not such as to warrant use of the Safety Car.

Deployment: The VSC procedure may be initiated to neutralise a TTCS upon the order of the Race Director. When the order is given, a message "VSC DEPLOYED" will be sent to all Competitors and all FIA light panels will display "VSC".

During a VSC Deployment: (a) No F1 Car may be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically, or in a potentially dangerous manner (whether on the track, Pit Entry Road, or Pit Lane); (b) All F1 Cars must reduce speed and stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU at least once in each marshalling sector and at both the first and second safety car lines; all F1 Cars must also be above this minimum time when FIA light panels change to green. When initiated during a TTCS, the stewards may impose a penalty on any driver who fails to stay above the minimum time. (c) No driver may overtake another F1 Car except: when entering pits (after reaching first safety car line); when leaving pits (before reaching second safety car line); whilst in Pit Entry Road, Pit Lane, or Pit Exit Road; or if any F1 Car slows with an obvious problem.

Use of Pit Lane during VSC: When initiated during a TTCS, no F1 Car may enter the pits whilst the VSC procedure is in use unless it is for the purpose of changing tyres.

Withdrawal of VSC: When the Race Director decides it is safe to end the VSC procedure, the message "VSC ENDING" will be sent to all Competitors and, at any time between 10 and 15 seconds later, "VSC" on the FIA light panels will change to green and drivers may continue the session or continue racing immediately. After 30 seconds the green lights will be extinguished. Each lap completed whilst the VSC procedure is in use during a TTCS will be counted as a lap.

topic: TTCS — Safety Car (SC)
text:
The Safety Car will be used only if Competitors or officials are in immediate physical danger on or near the track, but the circumstances are not such as to necessitate suspending the TTCS.

Deployment: The Safety Car may be brought into operation to neutralise a TTCS upon the order of the Race Director.
