When the order is given to deploy, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all Competitors, all FIA light panels will display "SC", all marshal's posts will display waved yellow flags and "SC" boards, and the Safety Car will join the track with its orange lights illuminated regardless of where the leader is.

During a SC Deployment: (a) No F1 Car may be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically, or in a potentially dangerous manner; (b) All F1 Cars must reduce speed and form up in a queue behind the Safety Car no more than the maximum allowable gap of ten (10) car lengths apart. From the time all Competitors have been sent the "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" message until the time each F1 Car crosses the first safety car line for the second time, drivers must stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU at least once in each marshalling sector and at both the first and second safety car lines. The stewards may impose a penalty on any driver who fails to stay above the minimum time. Once behind the Safety Car, the first F1 Car in line must stay less than the maximum allowable gap of ten (10) car lengths behind it. In poor visibility conditions, the Race Director may increase the maximum allowable gap to twenty (20) car lengths; the message "LOW VISIBILITY – MAXIMUM GAP TWENTY CAR LENGTHS" will be sent. (c) No driver may overtake another F1 Car or the Safety Car until they pass the Line for the first time after the Safety Car has entered the Pit Entry Road to return to the Pit Lane, with exceptions for: if signalled to do so from the Safety Car (by green light); under Articles B5.10.6, B5.10.8, B5.13.4c, and B5.15.3; when entering pits after the first safety car line; when leaving pits before the second safety car line; when the Safety Car is returning to pits and has reached the first safety car line; whilst in the Pit Entry Road, Pit Lane, or Pit Exit Road; any F1 Car stopping in its Designated Garage Area whilst the Safety Car is using the Pit Lane; or if any F1 Car slows with an obvious problem.

No F1 Car may enter the pits whilst the Safety Car is deployed unless it is for the purpose of changing tyres (except when cars and the Safety Car are required to use the Pit Lane). Each lap completed while the Safety Car is deployed will be counted as a lap of the TTCS.

topic: TTCS — Safety Car Order and Withdrawal
text:
Order of Cars Behind the SC: When instructed by the Race Director, the green light on the Safety Car will be illuminated to signal F1 Cars between it and the leader that they are required to pass. Once all such cars have passed, the green light will be extinguished. If the Race Director considers track conditions are unsuitable for overtaking, the message "OVERTAKING WILL NOT BE PERMITTED" will be sent to all Competitors.

If the Race Director considers it safe, the message "LAPPED CARS MAY NOW OVERTAKE" will be sent, and the green light on the Safety Car will be illuminated to signal all F1 Cars that have been lapped by the leader that they are required to pass the F1 Cars on the lead lap and the Safety Car. This will only apply to F1 Cars that were lapped at the time they crossed the Line at the end of the lap during which they crossed the first safety car line for the second time after the Safety Car was deployed. Whilst they are overtaking, the cars on the lead lap must always stay on the racing line unless deviating is unavoidable. Having overtaken, these cars should proceed at an appropriate speed without overtaking and make every effort to take up position at the back of the queue behind the Safety Car. The Safety Car shall be used at least until the leader is behind it and all remaining F1 Cars are queued behind them. Unless the Race Director considers the presence of the Safety Car remains necessary, once the "LAPPED CARS MAY NOW OVERTAKE" message has been sent, the Safety Car will return to the pits at the end of the following lap.

Withdrawal of Safety Car: When the Race Director decides it is safe to end the Safety Car period, the message "SAFETY CAR IN THIS LAP" will be sent to all Competitors and the orange lights on the Safety Car will be extinguished. This is the signal that it will be entering the Pit Lane at the end of that lap. From the point the orange lights are extinguished, drivers must proceed at a pace which involves no erratic acceleration or braking nor any other manoeuvre which is likely to endanger other drivers or impede the restart. As the Safety Car is approaching the Pit Entry Road the SC boards will be withdrawn and, other than on the last lap of the TTCS, the yellow flags will be withdrawn and a green flag and/or green light panel will be displayed at the Line.

If the Safety Car is still deployed at the beginning of the last lap, or is deployed during the last lap, unless the Race Director deems the continued presence of the Safety Car after the end-of-session signal is required, it will enter the Pit Lane at the end of the lap and the F1 Cars must proceed to take the end-of-session signal without overtaking before the Line.

topic: TTCS — Suspension Procedures
text:
Suspension of a Starting Procedure: If at any time after the formation laps behind the Safety Car have commenced, track conditions are considered unsuitable to start the TTCS, the message "STARTING PROCEDURE SUSPENDED" will be sent to all Competitors, red flags will be shown at all marshal posts and at the line, and the orange lights on the start gantry will be illuminated. All F1 Cars must enter the Pit Lane behind the Safety Car. The first F1 Car to arrive in the Pit Lane should proceed directly to the Pit Lane exit (unless an alternative location has been defined by the Race Director). All the other F1 Cars should form up in a line behind the first F1 Car in the order they entered the Pit Lane. All cars must stay in the Fast Lane.

Suspension of a TTCS: If the Race Director deems it necessary to suspend a TTCS, the message "RED FLAG - SPRINT SUSPENDED" or "RED FLAG - RACE SUSPENDED" will be sent, red flags will be shown at all marshal posts and at the Line, and the orange lights on the start gantry will be illuminated. When the signal is given: (a) Overtaking is forbidden; (b) The Pit Lane exit will be closed, and all F1 Cars must proceed slowly into the Pit Lane. The TTCS nor the timekeeping system will stop. However, the length of the Sprint suspension (per Article B2.3.3b) or the length of the Race suspension (per Article B2.5.3b) will be added to the maximum time period. If the TTCS cannot be resumed, the results will be taken at the end of the penultimate lap before the lap during which the signal to suspend the TTCS was given.

Provisions Applicable During a Suspension: F1 Cars may be worked on once they have stopped in the Fast Lane, but any such work is restricted to: starting the engine and any directly associated preparation; the addition of compressed gases (Article C4.5); the fitting or removal of permitted cooling and heating devices; changes to the air ducts around the front and rear brakes; changes to the radiator ducts; changes made for driver comfort; changing wheels and tyres; repair of genuine accident damage; in accordance with Article C3.10.10, adjustment of the position (not controlled by the FIA Standard ECU) of the Front Wing Profiles (no parts may be added, removed, or replaced); if a Heat Hazard has been declared, the cooling medium used in the Driver Cooling System may be replenished or replaced. Only team members, officials, and accredited television cameramen will be permitted in the Pit Lane. Unless asked to do so by the FIA, F1 Cars may not be moved from the Fast Lane during a suspension.

topic: TTCS — Resumption Procedure
text:
As soon as a resumption time is known, all Competitors will be informed using the OMS. In all cases at least ten (10) minutes warning will be given. Signals will be shown ten (10) minutes, five (5) minutes, three (3) minutes, one (1) minute, and fifteen (15) seconds before the resumption, each accompanied by an audible warning.

Ten (10) minute signal: if the Race Director deems it necessary, the use of wet-weather tyres is compulsory. Five (5) minute signal: the Safety Car orange lights will be illuminated and the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS ON" will be sent. All F1 Cars must have their wheels fitted. Tyre blankets must be disconnected from any power supply. After this signal, wheels may only be removed if the F1 Car has been moved out of the Fast Lane or during a further suspension. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver whose F1 Car did not have all its wheels fully fitted at the five (5) minute signal or has any of its wheels changed before it leaves the Pit Lane for the first time after the resumption time.

In the case of a resumption following the suspension of a TTCS, two (2) minutes prior to the resumption, any F1 Cars between the Safety Car and the leader, in addition to any F1 Cars that had been lapped by the leader at the time the TTCS was suspended, will be allowed to leave the Pit Lane, complete a further lap without overtaking, enter the Pit Lane, and re-join the line of F1 Cars in the Fast Lane. One (1) minute signal: the Safety Car will leave the Pit Lane and proceed to its resumption position on track. Unless otherwise defined by the Race Director, such resumption position will be at the end of the first timing sector.

All team personnel must leave the Fast Lane by the time the fifteen (15) second signal is given. At the resumption time the pit exit will be opened, all cars should leave the Pit Lane and proceed around the track to meet the Safety Car at its resumption position. The Safety Car will remain on track until such time as the Race Director decides it is safe to undertake a standing start resumption or rolling start resumption.

Standing Start Resumption: message "STANDING START" will be sent, FIA light panels will display "SS", the Pit Lane exit will be closed, and the Safety Car orange lights will be extinguished. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to resume the TTCS from the Pit Lane when required. Rolling Start Resumption: message "ROLLING START" will be sent, FIA light panels will display "RS", the Pit Lane exit will be closed, and the Safety Car orange lights will be extinguished. No driver may overtake another F1 Car on the track until they pass the Line for the first time after the Safety Car has returned to the Pit Lane.

topic: TTCS — Finishing Procedure
text:
A chequered flag will be the end-of-session signal and will be shown at the Line as soon as the leading F1 Car has covered the full distance.

Should for any reason the end-of-session signal be given before the leading F1 Car completes the scheduled number of laps, or the prescribed time has been completed, the TTCS will be deemed to have finished when the leading F1 Car last crossed the Line before the signal was given. Should the end-of-session signal be delayed for any reason, the TTCS will be deemed to have finished when it should have finished.

After receiving the end-of-session signal all F1 Cars must proceed on the circuit directly to the parc fermé without any unnecessary delay, without receiving any object whatsoever and without any assistance (except that of the marshals if necessary). An exception will be made for the winning driver of the Race who may perform an act of celebration before reaching parc fermé, provided any such act: (a) is performed safely and does not endanger other drivers or any officials; (b) does not call into question the legality of their F1 Car; (c) does not delay the podium ceremony. Any classified F1 Car which cannot reach the parc fermé under its own power will be placed under the exclusive control of the marshals who will take the F1 Car to the parc fermé.

topic: Tyre Limitations — Supply of Tyres
text:
The single tyre manufacturer (the "Tyre Supplier") appointed by the FIA must undertake to provide at each Competition: three (3) specifications of dry-weather tyre, one (1) specification of intermediate tyre, and one (1) specification of wet-weather tyre. Each must be visibly distinguishable from one another when a car is on the track.

At certain Standard Format Competitions, one additional specification of dry-weather tyre may be made available to all Competitors for the purpose of in-competition tyre evaluation ("ICTE"). At a maximum of two Standard Format Competitions, additional specifications of dry-weather tyres may be made available for in-competition tyre testing ("ICTT"). Should either of these Competitions be found to be unsuitable for effective evaluation of these tyres (due to weather or other issues), additional dry-weather tyres may be made available at a third Competition.

Information Prior to a Competition: Four (4) weeks prior, the FIA will provide whether additional tyre specifications will be allocated for ICTT. Two (2) weeks prior: (i) which tyre specifications will be made available for the Competition; (ii) the mandatory dry-weather tyre specification(s) for the Race, up to a maximum of two (2); (iii) the mandatory dry-weather tyre specification for Q3, such specification always being the softest of the three (3) specifications made available for the Competition. One (1) week prior: whether an additional specification of tyres will be made available for ICTE.

Tyres received by competitors from the Tyre Supplier may not be used on any rig, simulator or vehicle, other than the F1 Car for which they were intended.

topic: Tyre Limitations — Control and Allocation
text:
Other than in cases of force majeure (accepted as such by the stewards), all tyres intended for use at a Competition must be presented to the Technical Delegate for allocation prior to the start of the Competition.

A complete set of tyres will be deemed to comprise two (2) front and two (2) rear tyres, all of which must be of the same specification. The Technical Delegate will allocate sets of tyres to each driver from among the stock of tyres the Tyre Supplier makes available.

For each Competition, the number of sets of each specification and type of tyre allocated to each driver is as follows:

Standard Format Competition: Dry Hard – 2, Dry Medium – 3, Dry Soft – 8, Intermediate – 5, Wet – 2.
Alternative Format Competition: Dry Hard – 2, Dry Medium – 4, Dry Soft – 6, Intermediate – 6, Wet – 2.
Standard Format Competition with ICTT: Dry Hard – 2, Dry Medium – 3, Dry Soft – 7, Intermediate – 5, Wet – 2.
Note: For Monaco, each driver will be allocated three (3) sets of wet-weather tyres.

The outer sidewall of all tyres which are to be used at a Competition must be marked with a unique identification. The use of tyres without appropriate identification may result in a Race grid position penalty or disqualification from the Race as appropriate. The Technical Delegate may, at their absolute discretion, select alternative tyres to be used by any Competitor from among the stock the Tyre Supplier has present at the Competition. A Competitor wishing to replace one unused tyre by another identical unused one must present both tyres to the Technical Delegate.

topic: Tyre Limitations — Use and Return
text:
The only sets of tyres which may be used during a Competition are those defined in the allocation provisions, and each driver must only use tyres allocated and made available to them. Any driver who uses a set of tyres of differing specifications or tyres not allocated to them during a TTCS may not cross the Line on the track more than twice before returning to the pits and changing them. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who does not change tyres as specified.

Tyres fitted in the Pit Lane will be deemed to have been used once the F1 Car's timing transponder has shown that it has left the Pit Lane with these tyres fitted. Tyres fitted on the grid will be deemed to have been used when the car leaves its grid position under its own power with these tyres fitted.

All tyres must be used as complete sets. However, sets of the same specification may be mixed after Qualifying.

For each Competition, the maximum number of sets of each type of tyres that may be used by each driver: Standard Format Competition: Dry-Weather – 13, Intermediate – 5, Wet – 2; Alternative Format Competition: Dry-Weather – 12, Intermediate – 5, Wet – 2; Standard Format Competition with ICTT: Dry-Weather – 12, Intermediate – 5, Wet – 2. For Monaco, maximum is three (3) sets of wet-weather tyres.

During any free practice session, intermediate and wet-weather tyres may only be used after the track has been declared wet by the Race Director, following which intermediate, wet, or dry-weather tyres may be used for the remainder of the session.

Unless they have used intermediate or wet-weather tyres during the Race, each driver must use at least two (2) different specifications of dry-weather tyres during the Race, at least one (1) of which must be a mandatory dry-weather Race tyre specification. For Monaco, each driver must also use at least three (3) sets of tyres of any specification during the race. Unless the Race is suspended and cannot be re-started, failure to comply will result in disqualification of the relevant driver from the Race results.

If the formation lap(s) is started behind the Safety Car with compulsory wet-weather tyres, or the TTCS is resumed with wet-weather tyres, the use of wet-weather tyres until the Safety Car orange lights are extinguished and it returns to the Pit Lane is compulsory. A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver whose tyre(s) are changed for a different specification or who uses any other specification of tyres whilst the Safety Car is on the track at such times.

topic: Tyre Limitations — Dry-Weather Tyre Return Procedures (Standard Format)
text:
At each Standard Format Competition (where additional tyres are not made available for ICTT):

(i) One (1) set of the mandatory Q3 tyre specification may not be used nor returned before Q3, and for F1 Cars that qualified for Q3, one set of the same specification must be electronically returned no later than the covers-on time defined in Article B3.4.3.

(ii) Two (2) sets of the mandatory Race specification(s) may not be returned before the Race. For the avoidance of doubt, if there are two (2) mandatory Race tyre specifications, one (1) set of each specification may not be returned before the Race.

(iii) Two (2) sets must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP1.

(iv) Two (2) further sets must be electronically returned no later than two hours after the end of FP2, unless both FP1 and FP2 are either declared wet or cancelled, in which case one of these sets may be retained by each driver but must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP3.

(v) Two (2) further sets must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP3.

Regarding Intermediate and Wet-Weather Tyres in Standard Format: if FP1, FP2, or FP3 is declared wet, one (1) set of intermediate tyres must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP3.

topic: Tyre Limitations — Dry-Weather Tyre Return Procedures (Alternative Format)
text:
At each Alternative Format Competition:

(i) One (1) set must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP1.

(ii) One (1) set must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of the Sprint. For any driver who used a set during the Sprint, this must be the set with the highest number of laps completed in the Sprint.

(iii) Three (3) sets must be electronically returned no later than the covers-on time after Qualifying, defined in Article B3.4.3.

(iv) In each of the periods SQ1 and SQ2 of Sprint Qualifying, up to one set may be used, and this must only be a new set of the medium specification.

(v) In the period SQ3 of Sprint Qualifying, up to one set may be used, and this must only be a set of the soft specification.

Regarding Intermediate and Wet-Weather Tyres in Alternative Format: A maximum of one (1) additional set of intermediate tyres will be made available, and may be used by each driver, under the following circumstances: (A) If either FP1 or the Sprint Qualifying are declared wet, one (1) additional set of intermediate tyres will be made available to any driver who used a set of intermediate tyres during either session. Under such circumstances, one (1) used set of intermediate tyres must be electronically returned no later than the covers-on time after the end of Sprint Qualifying. (B) One (1) additional set of intermediate tyres will be made available to any driver who used a set during the Sprint and who was not previously allocated an additional set. Under such circumstances, this set may not be used before the pit exit is opened before the start of the Race, and one (1) set of used intermediate tyres must be electronically returned no later than the covers-on time after Qualifying.

topic: Tyre Return Procedure
text:
The official return of tyres will be made electronically using the FIA Race Team Client. In the event of an issue with the system, and when instructed to do so by the FIA, each Competitor will be requested to provide the tyre return data in a CSV file format via email.

Any set of electronically returned tyres must also be physically returned to the Tyre Supplier before the start of the following session.

Once all tyres have been returned electronically after the end of each day of on track activity, the Tyre Supplier will publish a list of the tyres which each driver has available to them for the remainder of the Competition.

Specific Provisions for ICTE: In addition to the specifications of dry-weather tyres allocated, at a Standard Format Competition where ICTE is scheduled, a maximum of two (2) sets of an additional evaluation specification of dry-weather tyres will be allocated to each driver. Each driver may use these tyres during FP1 and FP2. All additional tyres allocated for ICTE must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP2.

Specific Provisions for ICTT: In addition to the specifications of dry-weather tyres allocated, at a Standard Format Competition where ICTT is scheduled, additional sets of test specification dry-weather tyres will be allocated to each driver. If additional test specifications are made available for ICTT, these tyres must be used by each Driver during FP2. If FP2 is unsuitable for evaluation of these tyres (such as due to poor weather), they will not be made available and may be carried over to the back-up Competition. Unless additional tyres for ICTT have not been made available, or the session is declared wet, all Drivers must use these tyres during FP2 according to run plans specified by the Tyre Supplier, and the only dry weather tyres that may be used during FP2 are those allocated for ICTT. Drivers participating in ICTT must be eligible for a Full Super Licence and must have competed in at least one (1) Formula 1 Competition during their careers. All additional tyres allocated for ICTT must be electronically returned no later than two (2) hours after the end of FP2.

topic: Driver Adjustable Bodywork (DAB)
text:
The permitted "Driver Adjustable Bodywork" includes the adjustment of the incidence of the Front Wing Profiles controlled by the FIA Standard ECU (as described in Article C3.10.10) and the adjustment of the incidence of the RW Flap controlled by the FIA Standard ECU (as described in Article C3.11.6).

Driver Adjustable Bodywork will be considered deactivated when both the Front Wing Profiles and RW Flap are in their respective Corner Mode positions. It will be considered fully activated when, following command from the driver, both the Front Wing Profiles and RW Flap are in their respective Straight-Line Mode positions. It will be considered partially activated when, following command from the driver, the Front Wing Profiles are in their Straight-Line Mode position, and the RW Flap is in its Corner Mode position.

The FIA will provide all Competitors with relevant information regarding the defined Activation Zones for a circuit (including Activation Zones for full activation and Low Grip Activation Zones for partial activation only) no less than four (4) weeks prior to the start of the relevant Competition. The start of each defined Activation Zone shall be marked by signage on at least one (1) side of the circuit.

Use of the Driver Adjustable Bodywork: The driver may only activate (fully or partially) the Driver Adjustable Bodywork when they have been notified via the Control Electronics (Article C8.2) that it is enabled. For reasons of safety, the Race Director may, at any time and at their sole discretion, disable full activation of the Driver Adjustable Bodywork, allowing only partial activation in the associated Low Grip Activation Zones at such times. The Race Director may, at any time and at their sole discretion, subsequently re-enable full activation when they consider it is safe to do so. The use of full activation may only be re-enabled during any of the three periods of Sprint Qualifying or Qualifying when there is more than five (5) minutes remaining in the relevant period.

topic: Energy Deployment Limitations — Overtake Override Mode
text:
The absolute limits of electrical DC power of the ERS-K used to propel the F1 Car are defined in Article C5.2.8, and the limits of allowable energy harvested by the ERS-K Recharge are defined in Article C5.2.10. No less than four (4) weeks prior to the start of a Competition, the FIA will provide all Competitors with information and limitations applicable to the Competition, including: any adjustment(s) of the maximum electrical DC power of the ERS-K; the maximum energy that may be harvested by the ERS-K Recharge on a single lap during track running sessions other than TTCS; the maximum energy that may be harvested on a single lap of any TTCS when Overtake Override Mode is not active; the additional energy that may be harvested on any lap of any TTCS when Overtake Override Mode is enabled and activated; the value (time) of the "Detection Gap"; the position (lap distance) of the "Detection Line"; the position (lap distance) of the "Activation Line". The number of Competitions in which Article C5.2.10ii may apply will be limited to a maximum of 8 per Championship.

Enabling and Disabling: Prior to the start of any LTCS, Overtake will be enabled. Prior to the start or resumption of any TTCS, the Overtake Override Mode system will be disabled; it will be enabled when the leader has crossed the Detection Line for the first time after the start or resumption of the TTCS. When the Safety Car is deployed, the Overtake Override Mode system will be disabled; it will be enabled after all F1 Cars have crossed the Line after the Safety Car has entered the Pit Entry Road to return to the Pit Lane. For reasons of safety, the Race Director may, at any time and at their sole discretion, disable Overtake. The Race Director may subsequently re-enable Overtake when they consider it is safe to do so.

Activation and Deactivation: The driver may only use Overtake Override Mode when they have been notified via the Control Electronics that it is enabled and activated. During any LTCS, Overtake Override Mode will be activated at all times when it is enabled and may be used by the driver at any time. During any TTCS: Overtake Override Mode will be activated at the Activation Line, and may be used by the driver, when their F1 Car was less than the Detection Gap behind another F1 Car when they crossed the Detection Line. Overtake Override Mode will be deactivated when the driver crosses the Activation Line whilst it is activated, when their F1 Car was greater than the Detection Gap behind another F1 Car at the Detection Line.

topic: Car and Component Limitations
text:
Each Competitor may have no more than two (2) F1 Cars available for use at any one time during a Competition, except when all the following circumstances are met: (a) An F1 Car has suffered genuine accident damage or a significant failure or fault necessitating a change of survival cell; (b) The Competitor has provided a written request to the FIA to change the survival cell, and this has been approved by the Technical Delegate; (c) There are no more than two (2) F1 Cars available for one driver at any one time, and this period is only sufficient to facilitate the change of F1 Car.

Power Unit Limitations: In each Championship (unless a driver drives for more than one Competitor), each driver may use no more than: 3 engines (ICE); 3 turbochargers (TC); 3 exhaust sets (EXH) — each of the four elements (left-hand primaries, right-hand primaries, left hand secondary, right hand secondary) constituting an Exhaust set will be considered separately; 2 energy store units (ES); 2 of each control electronics units (PU-CE); 2 MGU-K; 5 of each Power Unit ancillary components (PU-ANC).

Each driver will be permitted to use an additional unit for each of the Power Unit elements in the 2026 Championship if the Power Unit used is supplied by a PU Manufacturer who has not supplied Power Units in 2026 and is in its first year of supplying Power Units.

Should a driver use more Power Unit elements than the numbers prescribed, a grid place penalty will be imposed upon them at the first Competition during which each additional element is used: (a) The first time an additional element of each type is used: Ten (10) grid place penalty for the race; (b) The next times an additional element of each type is used: Five (5) grid place penalty for the race. Penalties are cumulative.

Any of the elements listed will be deemed to have been used once the F1 Car's timing transponder has shown that it has left the Pit Lane. During any single Competition, if a driver introduces more than one of the same Power Unit element which is subject to penalties, only the last element fitted may be used at subsequent Competitions without further penalty.

topic: Power Unit Sealing and Usage Between Competitions
text:
After consultation with the relevant Power Unit Manufacturer, the FIA will attach seals to each of the relevant elements of the Power Unit prior to them being used for the first time at a Competition, to ensure that no significant parts can be rebuilt or replaced. Only PU elements which are not fitted to a car may be sealed. The ESME will be sealed by the FIA to prevent free access to the ES and PU-CE parts located inside the ESME.

Within two hours of the end of the post-Race parc fermé, additional seals will be applied to all used ICE, TC, and MGU-K elements to ensure they cannot be run or dismantled between Competitions. The sealing method must be agreed with the Technical Delegate.

Upon request to the FIA, these additional seals will be removed fifty (50) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 at the next Competition at which the Power Unit elements are required. All such Power Unit elements must remain within the Competitor's Designated Garage Area when not fitted to an F1 Car.

Following the removal of these additional seals, no Power Unit may be cranked (other than by hand) or started prior to twenty-six (26) hours before the scheduled start of FP1. At the first Competition of the Championship, and at the sole discretion of the Technical Delegate, once the sealing process is complete, permission to crank or start a Power Unit before this time may be granted.

At no time may a Power Unit be cranked (other than by hand) or started during a Competition when not fitted to an F1 Car eligible to participate in the Competition.

For safety reasons, the committed ES and PU-CE may be used between competitions provided the absolute DC electrical power is below 5kW. Exceptionally and solely for safety reasons, the FIA in its sole discretion may grant permission to a competitor to run a used unit without restricted conditions; in such case the FIA will inform the other PUMs.

If any of the FIA seals are damaged or removed from the relevant components within the Power Unit after they have been used for the first time, those parts may not be used again unless they were removed under FIA supervision.

topic: Personnel Limitations
text:
All persons concerned in any way with an entered F1 Car or present in any other capacity in the paddock, Pit Lane, or track during a Competition must always wear an appropriate pass. No pass may be issued or used other than with the agreement of the FIA. A pass may be used only by the person and for the purpose for which it was issued.

Operational Personnel: At each Competition during the period beginning twenty-nine (29) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 and ending two (2) hours after the start of the Race, each Competitor may not have more than a total of sixty (60) "Operational Personnel" who are associated in any way with the operation of the F1 Cars within the confines of the circuit. However, during the period starting forty-five (45) minutes before the start of the first formation lap until fifteen (15) minutes after the scheduled start of the Race, the number of such Operational Personnel is unlimited. Race drivers and staff whose duties are solely connected with hospitality, marketing, media, security, or driving trucks to or from the Competition are not considered Operational Personnel.

Trainee Personnel: In addition to the sixty (60) Operational Personnel, each Competitor will be permitted sixteen (16) individual exceptions during a Championship for "Trainee Personnel". However, no individual trainee may attend more than three (3) Competitions in this capacity.

Declaration of Personnel: A list of all operational, trainee, shared, and employee guest personnel must be submitted to the FIA prior to the start of Restricted Period One using the DMS and the official template provided by the FIA. Amendments after the start of Restricted Period One shall be permitted at the sole discretion of the FIA. A list of all personnel exempt from the provisions of Articles B9.2 or B9.3 who have been working on behalf of the Competitor within the restricted areas of the circuit during the Competition must be submitted to the FIA prior to the end of the Competition.

topic: Restricted Periods
text:
At each Competition, Operational Personnel and Trainee Personnel are not permitted within the confines of the circuit during the Restricted Periods.

"Restricted Period One": Commencing forty-two (42) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1 and ending twenty-nine (29) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1.

"Restricted Period Two": Commencing eighteen (18) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1 and ending four (4) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1.

"Restricted Period Three": At each Standard Format Competition, commencing fourteen (14) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP3 and ending three (3) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP3. If the unrestricted time between the end of FP2 and the start of the third restricted period exceeds four (4) hours, the excess will be added to the start of the third restricted period. At each Alternative Format Competition, commencing fourteen (14) hours prior to the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Sprint and ending three (3) hours prior to the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Sprint. If the unrestricted time between the end of Sprint Qualifying and the start of the third restricted period exceeds three (3) hours, the excess will be added to the start of the third restricted period.

Operational and Trainee Personnel will be permitted to: enter the Paddock thirty (30) minutes prior to the end of each Restricted Period for the sole purpose of easing congestion at the turnstiles; remain in the confines of the circuit for up to one (1) hour after the start of Restricted Period One and Two for exercise on the circuit, meals, and socialising; remain for up to thirty (30) minutes after the start of Restricted Period Three for exercise on the circuit, meals, and socialising. During these periods, personnel must not conduct operational activities.

Each Competitor will be permitted the following exceptions during the Championship: Restricted Period One: Six (6) exceptions; Restricted Period Two: Five (5) exceptions; Restricted Period Three: Four (4) exceptions. For the avoidance of doubt, these exceptions may not be used consecutively during a single Competition. In the case of a breach of this article, both drivers must start the Race from the Pit Lane.

Race drivers and personnel whose duties are solely connected with hospitality, marketing, media, security, or driving trucks to or from the Competition are exempt from these requirements. Such non-operational personnel may during each Restricted Period: load or unload (but not pack or unpack) freight; prepare equipment solely in support of other racing series; prepare the presentation of garages for display.

No later than 12 hours prior to the start of Restricted Period One, and at the sole discretion of the Race Director, following the failure of an official supplier to deliver the required services for the preparation of a Competition in a timely manner, an exception to Restricted Period One may be granted to all Competitors. In such circumstances this exception shall not be counted as one of the exceptions permitted under Article B9.5.3.

topic: Media Activities — Day Before On Track Running
text:
Day before on track running: Up to six drivers will be selected to participate in official media and promotional activities for a maximum duration of one (1) hour during a two (2) hour period, commencing 23 hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1. Any driver not taking part in an official FIA Press Conference must take part in a separate written media and broadcast session organised by their team. These separate media sessions will take place in time slots defined by the Media Delegate and must not be held at the same time as any official FIA Press Conference.

Within a one (1) hour period commencing 20 hours and 30 minutes prior to the scheduled start of FP1, six (6) drivers must be available for fan engagement activities for a maximum period of thirty (30) minutes each (this window includes the time required to travel to and from the fan activity). This time period may be subject to change according to specific event requirements; any changes will be communicated to the relevant Competitors no later than four (4) weeks in advance.

Each Competitor must provide a summary document to the Media Delegate listing the name and brief description of all major aerodynamic and bodywork components and assemblies that have not been run at a previous Competition or TCC and are intended to be run at the Competition. This summary document must be provided no later than twenty-three (23) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1. The contents will remain with the FIA and the Commercial Rights Holder and will not be provided to the media until one (1) hour before the start of the pre-event F1 Car display.

topic: Media Activities — First Day of On Track Running
text:
First day of on track running: Each Competitor must make both of its F1 Cars available outside their Designated Garage Area for the pre-event F1 Car display for a period of up to one (1) hour, which will commence no later than one and a half (1.5) hours prior to the start of FP1. Each F1 Car must be nominally complete and fitted with all major aerodynamic and bodywork components intended to be used when the F1 Car leaves the Pit Lane for the first time in FP1. Competitors may not prevent media from filming or photographing the F1 Cars during the F1 Car Presentation. Exceptions to the pre-event F1 Car display will be permitted with prior written approval of the Technical Delegate.

Each registered Power Unit Manufacturer must be available at one (1) Competition during the Championship to give a media presentation for a duration of at least 30 minutes. The Power Unit Manufacturer will be notified of the event at which it must give the presentation by the Media Delegate not later than four (4) weeks in advance.

Within a one (1) hour period finishing no later than one and a half (1.5) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP1, a maximum of twelve (12) drivers selected by the Media Delegate in consultation with the Commercial Rights holder must be available for fan engagement activities for a maximum period of thirty (30) minutes each.

At each Standard Format Competition, each Competitor must make one driver and one senior Competitor representative available to media in a format as defined by the Media Delegate for a minimum of five (5) minutes, within the one (1) hour and fifteen (15) minute period after the end of FP2 for drivers and within the one (1) hour and thirty (30) minute period after the end of FP2 for the senior Competitor representative. Competitors must ensure that each of their Championship Drivers participates in this media activity at least once in every two consecutive Competitions. Any Competitor using additional drivers during FP1 or FP2 must also make these drivers available to media during the same time frame.

At each Alternative Format Competition, all drivers who participate in Sprint Qualifying must make themselves available for media interviews immediately after the period in which they were eliminated.

A maximum of six (6) team representatives will be selected by the Media Delegate to participate in media activities for a period of one (1) hour, one (1) hour after the scheduled end of FP1. Each Competitor must have at least four (4) senior Competitor representatives to take part in these media activities during the Championship, comprising as a minimum the Team CEO (where applicable), Team Principal, and Technical Director.

topic: Media Activities — Second and Third Day of On Track Running
text:
Second day of on track running: Within a one (1) hour period finishing no later than one and a half (1.5) hours prior to the scheduled start of FP3 (or no later than one and a half (1.5) hours prior to the scheduled start of the formation lap for the Sprint for each Competition where a Sprint is scheduled), a maximum of twelve (12) drivers (who did not take part in fan activities on the first day) must be available for fan engagement activities for a maximum period of thirty (30) minutes each.

All drivers eliminated in Q1 or Q2 must make themselves available for media interviews immediately after being weighed following the end of the period in which they were eliminated. All drivers who participated in Q3 and who are not required to take part in the post-qualifying press conference must make themselves available for media interviews immediately after being weighed following Q3. Immediately after being weighed at the end of Qualifying, the three (3) highest classified drivers in Qualifying will take part in the post-qualifying procedures as prescribed in a Media Delegate's Note. For the duration of the TV pen interviews and post qualifying press conference, all drivers must remain attired in their respective teams' uniform only.

At each Alternative Format Competition: (i) any driver retiring before the end of the Sprint must make themselves available for media interviews after their return to the paddock; (ii) all drivers who finish the Sprint outside the top three (3) must make themselves available immediately after being weighed; (iii) immediately after being weighed following the Sprint, the three (3) highest classified drivers will be required to attend a press conference in the media centre for a maximum period of fifteen (15) minutes, then make themselves available for television interviews for a maximum period of fifteen (15) minutes.

Third day of on track running (Race day): All drivers must attend a thirty (30) minute drivers parade or presentation commencing two (2) hours before the scheduled start of the formation lap. All drivers must be present at the front of the grid for the playing of the national anthem no less than sixteen (16) minutes before the scheduled start of the formation lap. Any driver retiring before the end of the Race must make themselves available for media interviews after their return to the paddock. Immediately after being weighed following the Race, the three (3) highest classified drivers will take part in the post-race procedures. All drivers who finish the Race outside the top three (3) must make themselves available immediately after being weighed for media interviews. During the Race, each Competitor must make at least one (1) senior spokesperson available for interviews by officially accredited TV crews. Commencing one (1) and ending two (2) hours after the end of the Race, each Competitor must make one (1) senior spokesperson available to media at their team's hospitality for a minimum of five (5) minutes.

topic: Podium Ceremony
text:
The drivers finishing the Race in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd positions and a representative of the winning constructor must attend the prize-giving ceremony on the podium and abide by the podium procedure set out in Appendix B5 (except Monaco); and immediately thereafter make themselves available for a period of one and a half (1.5) hours for the purpose of television interviews and the press conference in the media centre.

For the duration of the Podium Ceremony and post-Race interview procedure, the drivers finishing in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd positions must remain attired only in their Driving Suits, 'done up' to the neck, not opened to the waist. For the duration of the TV pen interviews and FIA Post Race Press Conference, all Drivers must remain attired in their respective teams' uniform only.

If no points are awarded, the podium ceremony will not take place. However, the television interviews will take place at the time the podium ceremony would have taken place.

Podium Ceremony Provisions: A master of ceremonies will be appointed by the FIA. Only four trophies will be presented (winning driver, a representative of the winning constructor, second driver, third driver). Trophies must be in the form of traditional cups showing the FIA Formula 1 World Championship official logo, the official name of the Competition, and the driver's position. Winner's and constructor's trophies must be no less than 50cm and no more than 65cm high. Second and third drivers' trophies must be no less than 35cm and no more than 45cm high. Maximum weight per trophy must not exceed 5kg. Only three persons should be on the podium to present the trophies; in exceptional circumstances the master of ceremonies may increase this to four. No police, bodyguards or persons not authorised by the master of ceremonies are allowed on the podium. The podium and steps should be covered in green or dark blue carpet.

topic: Track Running Outside a Competition — General and TCC
text:
Competitors must inform the FIA and all other Competitors of any planned TPC, PE, or DE at least seven (7) days before it is due to commence, such declaration being amendable up to 72 hours before it commences. Required information includes: precise specification of car(s) to be used; name(s) of driver(s); type of activity; date(s) and intended hours; purpose of the activity; circuit or venue. An FIA Observer may be appointed and may attend any TPC, PE, or DE.

Testing of Current Car (TCC) may only take place: Between the times of 09:00 and 19:00 for a maximum continuous duration of nine (9) hours (unless otherwise agreed by all participating Competitors, the FIA, and the Tyre Supplier for Out-of-Competition Tyre Testing); on circuits located in Europe (unless agreed by majority of Competitors and FIA, or for Out-of-Competition Tyre Testing); whilst a Championship Competition is not taking place. No type of automobile other than a Current Car is permitted on the track (except for Out-of-Competition Tyre Testing where Previous Cars and Mule Cars are also permitted). F1 Cars being driven by drivers who do not qualify for a Super Licence must be fitted with a blue main rear light which must be illuminated at all times the F1 Car is on the track.

TCC Opportunities: (a) Pre-Season Private Collective Testing: One (1) test, five (5) consecutive days between 5th and 31st January 2026, during which each Competitor may complete three (3) days of track running. Each Competitor may only use one (1) F1 Car on each day. A Competitor will be considered as having carried out a day of track running at the point their car leaves the Pit Lane for the first time during a day. (b) Pre-Season Public Collective Testing: Two (2) tests of three (3) consecutive days duration between 7 February and seven (7) days before the start of the first Competition. Each Competitor may only use one (1) F1 Car on each day. One (1) day may be set aside for testing of wet-weather tyres if requested by the Tyre Supplier. (c) Post-Season Test: One (1) test, one (1) day carried out on the circuit at which the last Competition of the Championship was held, commencing no less than thirty-six (36) hours after the end of the Competition. Each Competitor must use two (2) F1 Cars: one driven by drivers with Super Licences for the sole purpose of tyre specification testing for the following season, and one for the sole purpose of providing Young Drivers (who must hold an FIA International A Licence and must not have competed in more than two (2) Formula 1 World Championship Races during their career) with the opportunity to test current F1 Cars. (d) Out-of-Competition Tyre Testing: A maximum of forty (40) car days organised by the FIA in consultation with all Competitors and the Tyre Supplier, for the sole purpose of providing the Tyre Supplier with the chance to test improvements to the design of their tyres. Drivers must be eligible for a Full Super Licence and must have competed in at least one (1) Formula 1 Competition during their careers. (e) Substitute Driver Test: One (1) day, carried out between the start of a ten (10) day period which precedes the start of the second Competition and the last Competition of the Championship, in case a Competitor declares that one of its current Race drivers is to be substituted by a driver who has not participated in a Formula 1 World Championship Race in the two (2) previous calendar years.

topic: Track Running Outside a Competition — TPC, TMC, PE, DE
text:
Testing of Previous Car (TPC): TPC running may only take place for a maximum continuous duration of nine (9) hours between the times of 09:00 and 19:00. TPC may only be carried out with cars constructed to the specification of the period (components and software of a specification that have been used in at least one (1) Competition or TCC of a Championship season during the period used in the definition of a Previous Car). Exceptionally, and at the sole discretion and prior approval of the FIA, components and/or software may be fitted that do not comply, for cost, reliability, safety, lack of availability, or track condition reasons. Each Competitor may not have more than one (1) car available for the purpose of TPC and may not use more than one (1) car for the purpose of TPC during any day of TPC. TPC may only take place on circuits holding an FIA Grade 1 or FIA Grade 1T Circuit Licence, and may not take place on a circuit hosting a Competition in the Championship in the sixty (60) days prior to the start of the relevant Competition. Each Competitor may complete a maximum of twenty (20) days of TPC in each calendar year. Each Competitor may complete a maximum of one thousand (1000) kilometres of TPC in each calendar year using drivers entered in the Championship, accumulated over a maximum of four (4) of the days allowed.

Promotional Event (PE): Each Competitor will be permitted to carry out two (2) PE with a Current Car which will not be considered TCC. A PE must not exceed 200km and only one may be carried out per team per day. Only tyres manufactured specifically for this purpose by the Tyre Supplier may be used.

Demonstration Event (DE): At the sole discretion of the FIA, each Competitor will be permitted to carry out: two (2) DE's with a Current Car (not TCC); and DE's organised by the Commercial Rights Holder with a Current Car (not TCC). No DE using a Current Car may exceed 15km throughout the duration of the event. No DE using a Previous Car may exceed 50km. During any DE, cars must be fitted with the FIA ECU required by Article C8.3.

topic: Parc Fermé Permitted Works — Full List
text:
Parc Fermé Permitted Works (Appendix B2) — the complete list of work that may be carried out when a car is deemed to be in parc fermé:

BRAKES: Brake friction material may be removed, measured, de-glazed and refitted. The brake system may be bled.

BODYWORK: Adjustment of the position (not controlled by the FIA Standard ECU) of the Front Wing Profiles (no parts may be added, removed, or replaced). Bodywork (excluding radiators and heat exchangers) may be removed. Bodywork components may be inspected with the use of NDT methods provided no disassembly takes place. Cosmetic changes may be made to the bodywork and tape may be added. Any part of the car may be cleaned. Bodywork fixings and cable ties (consumable fasteners) may be replaced. Any bodywork component may be repaired where the damage is patched, bonded, or fixed together (repair must cause no more than incidental changes in bodywork geometry; no replacement components or sub-components may be used). The front wing, brake drums, and wheel nut retention caps may be changed for pitstop practice items, provided the original components stay in vision of the scrutineer and are refitted once pitstop practice is completed.

CLIMATIC CONDITIONS: If the Technical Delegate is satisfied that changes in climatic conditions necessitate alterations, a "CHANGE IN CLIMATIC CONDITIONS" message will be sent. From this point until the start of the subsequent sprint or race, changes may be made to: Components specified in Articles C3.14.4 and C3.15.5; Power unit and/or gearbox cooling bodywork within specified reference volumes; The settings of any bypass valves or flow restrictors in cooling systems; The addition or removal of the Driver Cooling Scoop.

DRIVER COMFORT: Changes to improve the driver's comfort (anything other than adjustment of mirrors, seat belts, and pedals may only be carried out with specific permission of the Technical Delegate). If ambient temperature changes significantly, Competitors will be requested to change the head padding. The addition or removal of padding is permitted (under supervision; must be removed before post-race weighing if required by the Technical Delegate). If a Heat Hazard has been declared, the cooling medium in the Driver Cooling System may be added, replenished, or replaced. If a Heat Hazard is declared and driver has elected not to wear any items of personal equipment that form part of the Driver Cooling System, the 0.5kg of ballast in the cockpit may be fitted under FIA Technical Delegate supervision.

ELECTRONICS: F1 on board cameras, team telemetry system components, voice radio components, marshalling system components, timing transponders, FIA ADR, high speed cameras and associated equipment may be removed, refitted, checked, or replaced if requested by the FIA-designated supplier. A jump battery may be connected and on-board electrical units may be freely accessed via physical connection. Safety checks including charging/discharging of ERS energy storage devices. Batteries for clutch disengagement system and/or fire extinguisher may be charged or replaced. The power supply to the onboard fire extinguisher may be disconnected (must be reconnected before the car exits the Pit Lane). Repair of an electronic component (e.g. damaged connector pin, wiring loom). Damaged sensor lenses may be replaced provided the actual sensor remains unchanged. Pitot tubes may be removed, cleaned, refitted, and functionality checked; may be covered or uncovered.

FLUIDS: Fuel may be drained or added. Compressed gases may be drained or added. Permitted breather, heating, or cooling devices may be fitted. Fluids may be drained and/or replenished (fluids used for replenishment must conform to the same specification as the original fluids). Drinking fluid for the driver may be added at any time (container capacity must not exceed 1.5 litres). System checks may be carried out on fluid systems, including taking fluid samples for analysis. Leak detection spray may be used to inspect fluid systems. Inboard and outboard suspension sphericals may be lubricated.

REPAIR OF GENUINE ACCIDENT DAMAGE: Damage sustained as a result of contact with a barrier; damage sustained as a result of contact with another car on track; damage incurred whilst off track limits which also result in significant loss of lap time or a lap time deleted by the Race Director.

POWERTRAIN: Engines may be started. Spark plugs may be removed for internal engine inspection and cylinder compression checks. The air intake filter upstream of the compressor may be inspected and cleaned. Inspection bungs may be removed for internal gearbox inspection (borescope; gearbox must not be disassembled from the car). The exhaust system may be inspected, including use of NDT methods.

TYRES: Wheels, wheel fasteners, and tyres may be removed, changed, or rebalanced. Tyre pressures may be adjusted.

GENERAL TASKS: The car may be weighed using an allocated tyre set (or a set of travel tyres; use of machined setup plates is not permitted). Exhaust extraction devices may be fitted whilst starting the engine in the garage.

SURVIVAL CELL: A change of car (as defined in Article B8.1.2) if that car has suffered genuine accident damage or a significant failure or fault necessitating a change of survival cell. All components of the replacement car must be the same in design and similar in mass, inertia, and function to the original. The set-up of the suspension must be the same.

WORK REQUIRED BY THE TECHNICAL DELEGATE: Any work requested by the Technical Delegate.

topic: Definitions
text:
Key definitions from Appendix B1:

"Alternative Format Competition" (AFC): any Competition where a Sprint is scheduled.
"Standard Format Competition" (SFC): any Competition where a Race is scheduled and a Sprint is not scheduled.
"Current Car" (CC): a car designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of the 2026 or subsequent Championships. No Competitor may sell or make available any such Current Car to any third party without prior authorisation of the FIA.
"Previous Car" (PC): a car designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of any of the 2022–2025 Championships. No Competitor may sell or make available any such Previous Car to any third party without prior authorisation of the FIA.
"Historic Car" (HC): a car designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations in force during the years preceding those referred to in the definition of a Previous Car.
"Mule Car" (MC): a car designed and constructed in order to comply with the Technical Section C of the FIA F1 Regulations or the technical regulations of any of the four (4) calendar years falling immediately prior to the calendar year of the Championship, but suitably modified for the purpose of providing the Tyre Supplier with a means of track testing of its future products or for providing the FIA with a means of testing components or systems for a future Championship. No Competitor may sell or make available any such Mule Car to any third party without prior authorisation of the FIA.
"Lap Time Classified Session" (LTCS): any track running session during which the classification of the session is determined based upon the time taken by a driver to complete a single lap. Includes free practice sessions, the sprint qualifying session and the qualifying session.
"Total Time Classified Session" (TTCS): any track running session during which the classification of the session is determined based upon the total time taken by a driver to complete a number of laps greater than one. Includes the Sprint session and the Race session.
"Testing of Current Car" (TCC): any track running time, not part of a Competition, in which a Competitor entered in the Championship participates (or in which a third party participates on behalf of a Competitor or a supplier of a homologated power unit), using a Current Car.
"Testing of Previous Car" (TPC): any track running time, not part of a Competition, using a Previous Car.
"Testing of Historic Car" (THC): any track running time, not part of a Competition, using a Historic Car.
"Testing of Mule Car" (TMC): any track running time, not part of a Competition, using a Mule Car.
"Demonstration Event" (DE): an event in which a Competitor participates purely for marketing or demonstration purposes.
"Promotional Event" (PE): an event in which a Competitor participates purely for marketing or promotional purposes using a Current Car.
"Official Messaging System" (OMS): the FIA official messaging system used as a means of real-time or near real-time communication to all Competitors during a Competition.
"Document Management System" (DMS): the FIA provided document management and exchange system used as the primary means of document exchange with Competitors during a Competition.
"Restricted Period" (RP): a period of time during which team personnel who are associated in any way with the operation of the F1 Cars are not permitted within the confines of the circuit.
"Fast Lane": The Pit Lane will be divided into two lanes. The lane closest to the pit wall will be designated the Fast Lane and may be no more than 3.5 metres wide.
"Inner Lane": The lane closest to the garages will be designated the Inner Lane.
"Pit Entry Road": unless otherwise defined by the Race Director, the section of track leading to the Pit Lane, between the first safety car line and the beginning of the Pit Lane.
"Pit Exit Road": unless otherwise defined by the Race Director, the section of track from the end of the Pit Lane leading to the track, between the end of the Pit Lane and the second safety car line.

topic: Approved Changes for 2027 and 2028
text:
Changes for 2027 (Appendix B56):

Personnel Limitations: At each Competition during the period beginning twenty-nine (29) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 and ending two (2) hours after the start of the Race, each Competitor may not have more than a total of fifty-nine (59) Operational Personnel.

Restricted Period Exceptions for 2027: Restricted Period One — Five (5) exceptions; Restricted Period Two — Four (4) exceptions; Restricted Period Three — Three (3) exceptions.

Track Running Changes for 2027: Pre-Season Public Collective Testing changes to one (1) test of three (3) consecutive days duration between 1 February and seven (7) days before the start of the first Competition. Out-of-Competition Tyre Testing has expanded provisions allowing F1 Cars at tests between the end of the first Competition and 31 December to satisfy one of two conditions: (a) comply with Technical Section C of FIA F1 Regulations of the Championship using components and software used in at least one Race or TCC during the current year or the year preceding; or (b) comply with Technical Section C of FIA F1 Regulations of the calendar year falling immediately prior to the calendar year of the Championship using components and software used in at least one Race or TCC during the year preceding the Championship.

Changes for 2028:

Personnel Limitations: At each Competition during the period beginning twenty-nine (29) hours before the scheduled start of FP1 and ending two (2) hours after the start of the Race, each Competitor may not have more than a total of fifty-eight (58) Operational Personnel.

Restricted Period Exceptions for 2028: Restricted Period One — Four (4) exceptions; Restricted Period Two — Three (3) exceptions; Restricted Period Three — Two (2) exceptions.

Definition Changes for 2028: "Current Car" (CC) is defined as a car which was designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of the Championship, or those of the preceding year's or the following year's Championship. "Previous Car" (PC) is defined as a car which was designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of any of the three (3) calendar years falling immediately prior to the calendar year preceding the year of the Championship.

topic: FIA F1 Regulations - Document Overview and Convention
text: The 2026 FIA Formula 1 General Regulatory Provisions is Issue 02, published on 23 February 2026, with WMSC approval on 27 February 2026. The document uses a color convention: Black text indicates unchanged content from Issue 01; Pink text indicates changes relative to Issue 01 approved by the WMSC on 27/02/26; Red text provides information on applicable Governance and relevant Advisory Committee; Orange text provides reference information on relevant FIA F1 Documents; Green text provides comments, explanations, or indications of further work that are non-binding and non-regulatory. The document is organized into Articles A1 through A9, plus Appendices A1 through A9.

topic: FIA F1 Regulations - Preamble and Core Objectives
text: The F1 Regulations are adopted to safeguard the fundamental values underpinning the FIA and the FIA Formula One World Championship. The core objectives (the Objectives) are: (a) maintain the Championship as the pinnacle of motorsport; (b) promote the highest safety standards; (c) promote and protect sporting fairness; (d) promote competitive balance and sustainability; (e) ensure long-term financial stability and sustainability of the Championship, its stakeholders, F1 Teams and PU Manufacturers; (f) promote environmental sustainability; (g) protect the image, reputation, and integrity of the Championship; and (h) preserve the unique technology, innovation, and engineering challenge of Formula One.

topic: Article A1 - General Principles: Overview
text: The FIA is responsible for the sporting organisation and regulation of the FIA Formula One World Championship, comprising FIA Formula One Grand Prix competitions included on the International Sporting Calendar (each a Competition), with two World Championship titles: one for Drivers and one for Constructors. The Championship is the exclusive property of the FIA, which has granted the Commercial Rights Holder the exclusive right to exploit commercial rights. Section A (General Regulatory Provisions) and its appendices include provisions of general application to the Championship that apply to all other sections of the FIA F1 Regulations unless stated otherwise.

topic: Article A1.2 - Applicable Regulations and FIA F1 Regulations Structure
text: The Championship and all F1 Activities are governed by FIA rules including the FIA Statutes, the FIA International Sporting Code (ISC), the FIA F1 Regulations, the FIA Code of Ethics, the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, and any other rules issued by the FIA. The FIA F1 Regulations comprise: Section A (General Regulatory Provisions); Section B (Sporting Regulations); Section C (Technical Regulations); Section D (Financial Regulations – F1 Teams); Section E (Financial Regulations – PU Manufacturers); Section F (Operational Regulations). Applicable Laws take precedence over FIA Rules and Regulations where they conflict, and there will be no breach of FIA Rules in such cases.

topic: Article A1.2.3 - FIA F1 Documents: Binding and Non-Binding
text: The FIA may issue additional FIA F1 Documents prefixed by FIA-F1-Doc, followed by document number, version, and title. Binding FIA F1 Documents are limited to: (i) Determinations under Financial Regulations; (ii) technical specifications for correct installation of components per Technical Regulations; (iii) mandatory information or documentation formats for compliance; (iv) urgent safety actions. Non-binding FIA F1 Documents include Technical Directives, Sporting Directives, interpretation and clarification documents, inspection details, requests for test actions, and operational instructions. Non-binding documents do not create additional compliance obligations beyond existing Regulations. FIA F1 Documents are ordinarily confidential, available only to FIA-designated recipients, though the FIA may publish them at its sole discretion.

topic: Article A1.3 - Application: Who is a Covered Person
text: Any Covered Person participating in the Championship, any Competition, or any F1 Activities is deemed to have agreed to be bound by and comply with the FIA Rules and Regulations and all Decisions, and to have submitted to the FIA's authority. Covered Persons include: F1 Teams and their Personnel; PU Manufacturers and their Personnel; Drivers; ASNs; Organisers; Promoters; Single Suppliers; Circuit Operators; Officials; New Entrant Teams (per A3.5); New Entrant PU Manufacturers (per A3.6); any other person captured by A1.4.1; and any person who agrees in writing to be bound by FIA Rules. Breaches of FIA Rules other than the FIA F1 Regulations by Covered Persons will be pursued under those specific rules breached.

topic: Article A1.4 - General Responsibility for Breaches
text: Each F1 Team, PU Manufacturer, and other entity is strictly liable for any non-compliance with FIA F1 Regulations resulting from actions of others acting on their behalf, including Personnel and any entity in their Legal Group. There is no individual liability under FIA F1 Regulations unless specifically stated. Where specific obligations are placed on individuals, those individuals may be personally liable in addition to the strict liability of the relevant F1 Team or PU Manufacturer. Financial Penalties will only be imposed on individuals if the individual is a Driver, or a Key Individual of an F1 Team or PU Manufacturer for breaches relating to their personal conduct under Section A and the ISC that fall outside Sections B, C, D, E, and F. In all other cases, Financial Penalties for individual actions are imposed on the F1 Team, PU Manufacturer, or organisation. Ignorance of FIA Rules and Regulations is not a defence to any breach.

topic: Article A2.1 - Format of the Championship
text: The FIA publishes the list of Competitions in the International Sporting Calendar prior to 1 January each year, each having the status of a restricted International Competition. The maximum number of Competitions is 24 and the minimum is eight. No more than 24 F1 Cars may participate, with two F1 Cars entered by each F1 Team. The Drivers' Championship title is awarded to the F1 Driver with the highest number of Championship points from all Competitions that took place. The Constructors' Championship title is awarded to the F1 Team with the highest combined points from both F1 Cars. If an F1 Team using a Power Unit it does not manufacture wins the Constructors' Championship, the title is awarded to the F1 Team. Tiebreaking is done by greatest number of first places, then second places, then third places, and so on through race results, then qualifying results.

topic: Article A2.2.1 - Championship Points System for Race Competitions
text: Points for both Drivers' and Constructors' Championships are awarded at each Competition based on final race classification and the number of laps completed by the leader. No points are awarded unless a minimum of two complete and consecutive laps have been completed by the leader without a Safety Car or Virtual Safety Car procedure. If the leader has completed 2 laps but less than 25% of Scheduled Race Distance (Col. 1): 1st=6, 2nd=4, 3rd=3, 4th=2, 5th=1. If 25% but less than 50% (Col. 2): 1st=13, 2nd=10, 3rd=8, 4th=6, 5th=5, 6th=4, 7th=3, 8th=2, 9th=1. If 50% but less than 75% (Col. 3): 1st=19, 2nd=14, 3rd=12, 4th=10, 5th=8, 6th=6, 7th=4, 8th=3, 9th=2, 10th=1. If 75% or more (Col. 4): 1st=25, 2nd=18, 3rd=15, 4th=12, 5th=10, 6th=8, 7th=6, 8th=4, 9th=2, 10th=1.

topic: Article A2.2.2 - Championship Points System for Sprint
text: Points for both Drivers' and Constructors' Championships are awarded at each Alternative Format Competition based on final Sprint classification and number of laps completed. No points are awarded unless a minimum of two complete and consecutive laps have been completed by the leader without a Safety Car or Virtual Safety Car procedure. If the leader has completed 2 laps but less than 50% of the Scheduled Sprint Distance, no points are awarded. If the leader has completed 50% or more of the Scheduled Sprint Distance, points are awarded: 1st=8, 2nd=7, 3rd=6, 4th=5, 5th=4, 6th=3, 7th=2, 8th=1. If the formation lap is started behind the Safety Car, the original Sprint session distance is deemed to be the distance calculated per Article B2.3.2a. Dead heat rule: prizes and points tied for the same position are added together and shared equally.

topic: Article A2.3 - F1 Car Livery Requirements
text: The ISC provisions on F1 Car livery do not apply to the Championship. Both F1 Cars entered by a team must be presented in substantially the same livery at every Competition. Any material change during a Championship may only be made with the agreement of the FIA and the Commercial Rights Holder per FIA-F1-DOC098. Political or religious advertising, or advertising prejudicial to FIA interests, is strictly prohibited. F1 Teams must ensure advertising complies with Applicable Laws. Each F1 Car must bear the FIA logo in blue or white with a height of at least 75mm, positioned on the top or either side of the nose, visible from the side. The car make name or emblem must appear on the front of the nose, at least 25mm in its largest dimension. The driver's name must appear on external bodywork, clearly legible. One car's on-board camera above the principal roll structure must remain as supplied; the other must be predominantly fluorescent yellow. Livery may not protrude beyond bodywork and must be substantially similar on both sides.

topic: Article A2.4 - Competition Numbers
text: All F1 Drivers are assigned a permanent Competition Number on a first come, first served basis, used at every Competition in a given Championship. Drivers may request a change in writing to the FIA before the Championship entry list is published, taking effect only in the following Championship. The reigning World Champion Driver may use the number one; their previously allocated number is reserved for them in the subsequent Championship if they do not retain the title. A driver permanently forfeits their Competition Number by confirming in writing to the FIA or by not participating for two consecutive Championships; the number becomes available the next Championship season. All Other Racing Drivers use Competition Numbers issued to the F1 Team by the FIA. Competition Numbers are 1 to 99 inclusive, with the exception of 17. Competition Numbers must be clearly visible from the front of the F1 Car with a minimum height of 160mm and minimum stroke thickness of 25mm.

topic: Article A2.5 and A2.6 - Postponement, Cancellation, and Prize Giving Ceremony
text: A Competition may be postponed or cancelled in accordance with the ISC, or if fewer than 12 F1 Cars are available. The F1 Drivers finishing first, second, and third in the Drivers' Championship, a representative of the first-place Constructors' Championship team, and a running or static version of the winning car must be present for the duration of the annual FIA Prize Giving Ceremony and Gala Dinner, at the F1 Team's cost. Failure to comply results in a fine of up to €250,000 per failure, except in case of Force Majeure, payable to the FIA per the ISC. The Constructors' Championship Trophy and Drivers' Championship Trophy are presented at the FIA Prize Giving Ceremony and Gala Dinner, subject to Appendix A8 requirements.

topic: Article A3.1 - F1 Team Entry Applications
text: Existing and New Entrant F1 Teams must submit applications prior to each Championship edition. Applications for Championship Year N may be submitted 21 October to 1 November of Year N-1, and must include: Entry Form (Appendix A4A); registration form for key Personnel (Appendix A4B); F1 Team Super Licence application; and an undertaking to pay the Entry Fee by 15 December of Year N-1. Late applications are considered only on payment of a late entry fee; the FIA notifies the applicant within 30 days. Applications must include: confirmation of compliance with FIA Rules; the team name (must include chassis name); Power Unit make; F1 Car make (if using a third-party PU, car name must combine team name and PU Manufacturer name, team first); driver names; and an undertaking to participate in every Competition with both cars. The FIA publishes the list of accepted F1 Cars and drivers with Competition Numbers on or before 20 December of Year N-1. Successful applicants are automatically entered in all Competitions.

topic: Article A3.2 - Power Unit Manufacturer Entry Applications
text: Any PU Manufacturer registered to supply Power Units to F1 Teams in the 2026 to 2030 Championships must submit a Power Unit homologation dossier to the FIA before 1 March of the first year it intends to supply. The homologation is valid until the end of the 2030 Championship unless a substantive change to PU Regulations requires a new dossier. The dossier may be updated per the process in Appendix C5 of Section C.

topic: Article A3.3 - Licences
text: F1 Drivers must hold a valid Super Licence and International Licence; free practice drivers must hold a valid Free Practice Only Super Licence and International Licence per the ISC and Appendix L. When a penalty other than a reprimand or fine is imposed, Stewards may add penalty points to a driver's Super Licence. Accumulation of 12 penalty points results in a one-Competition suspension, after which 12 points are removed. Penalty points remain for 12 months from imposition. F1 Teams must hold a valid Super Licence as a condition of entry, renewed annually by the Entry Form deadline. Organisers and specified Officials (Stewards, race directors, clerks of the course, medical delegates, deputy medical delegates, technical delegates, media delegates, timekeepers, Safety Car drivers, masters of ceremonies, and any other FIA-specified Officials) must each hold a valid Super Licence, renewed annually.

topic: Article A3.4 to A3.6 - Registration, New Entrant Teams, New Entrant PU Manufacturers
text: F1 Teams and PU Manufacturers must register key Personnel with the FIA per ISC Articles 2.6.4 and 2.6.5 and Appendices A4B and A5. New Entrant Teams must comply with Section A, Section B (Article B11), Section D, and Section F (Articles F1, F2, F3.1, F4) for the complete Year N-1 before participating in Year N, and must pass the Fit and Proper Persons Test. New Entrant PU Manufacturers for Year N must comply with Section A for complete Years N-4 through N-1; Section E for N-3 through N-1; Section F Articles F3.2, F5.1, F5.2, F5.3.2 for N-4 through N-1; and F5.3.3 for Year N-1. The deadline for a New Entrant PU Manufacturer registration form is 30 June of Year N-4. Registration is only complete upon payment of the administrative fee, entry into the PU Manufacturer Non-Assert Agreement, and agreement to applicable governance processes. New Entrant PU Manufacturers must also pass the Fit and Proper Persons Test.

topic: Article A4 - Integrity Requirements
text: The Fit and Proper Persons Test (FPP Test) is set out in Appendix F to the ISC. It applies to any natural person (FP Relevant Person) within F1 Teams, New Entrant Teams, PU Manufacturers, and New Entrant PU Manufacturers who wishes to become or remain a Fit and Proper Person.
