FP Relevant Persons include: any natural person holding directly or indirectly 30% or more of outstanding shares; and any CEO, Team Principal, or person who Controls or determines the management of the entity. The FPP Test is conducted for new FP Relevant Persons and for existing FP Persons whose circumstances change to potentially trigger disqualifying conditions. The FIA adheres to the World Anti-Doping Code (since 2010), incorporated into FIA Anti-Doping Regulations. FIA Manipulation of Competition Regulations protect against efforts to improperly impact competition results. FIA Safeguarding Policy promotes wellbeing of all individuals, especially children and vulnerable adults. FIA Anti-Alcohol Regulations prohibit substances affecting behaviour, judgment, and driving ability.

topic: Article A5.1 - General Obligations Applicable to All Covered Persons
text: All Covered Persons must: comply with FIA Rules and Regulations at all times; respond to FIA requests and Demands by specified deadlines; submit required information by deadlines; cooperate fully and in a timely manner with FIA regulatory functions and investigations; not delay, impede, or frustrate FIA regulatory functions; not threaten or intimidate persons from good faith reporting of alleged breaches; not retaliate against witnesses; not sign or submit false or fraudulent information or Declarations; not submit inaccurate or misleading Reporting Documentation; comply with Decisions, ABAs, and settlements; comply with provisional suspensions or sanctions; perform obligations with honesty and integrity; not bring the FIA or Championship into disrepute; and comply with all other applicable obligations including ISC Article 12.2. Nothing in these obligations constitutes a waiver of legal rights including Legal Professional Privilege.

topic: Article A5.2 - FIA Roles and Responsibilities
text: The FIA is responsible for developing, administering, and enforcing the FIA Rules and Regulations and exercising the powers and functions set out therein. The FIA monitors compliance on an ongoing basis, investigates suspected non-compliance, and takes appropriate enforcement action. The Prosecuting Body or Cost Cap Administration conduct investigations; the FIA Single Seater Department or FIA Legal may also request information/access. References to the FIA in the context of Financial Regulations mean the Cost Cap Administration. References to the FIA shall not include Stewards, any FIA Court, or Judging Panel unless specifically stated. The FIA may engage Independent Audit Firms, Stewards, external control bodies, experts, external legal advisors, or other specialists; these persons receive remuneration from the FIA and are bound by confidentiality.

topic: Article A5.3 - Promoters and Organisers
text: The Commercial Rights Holder appoints a Promoter for each Competition. The Promoter is responsible for promoting the Competition and controls only financial and commercial matters, excluding Financial Regulations matters. The Promoter shall not intervene in safety, sporting, technical, or organisational matters during a Competition. The Promoter must procure third-party insurance for all Competitors, personnel, and drivers per FIA requirements; insurance details must be sent to the FIA no later than 90 days before the Competition; the policy must comply with national laws and FIA requirements; drivers are not third parties with respect to one another. The Organiser is proposed by the Promoter to the relevant ASN for FIA approval; the Organiser must be the ASN of the country or territory where the Competition takes place, or its nominee. No F1 Team or association of F1 Teams may organise, promote, or be associated with an ASN for the organisation of a Competition to prevent competitive advantage. However, an independently managed affiliate of an F1 Team may be a Promoter or Circuit Operator, and an F1 Team or its holding companies may sponsor a Competition or Circuit.

topic: Article A5.4 to A5.6 - ASNs, Circuit Operators, and Officials
text: ASNs are FIA members responsible for exercising Sporting Power across one national territory. Within their territories, ASNs have authority for issuing International Licences, homologating Circuits, and payment of the Calendar Fee. Circuit Operators are responsible for the Circuit where a Competition takes place, must comply with terms and conditions of the Circuit licence issued by the FIA and any requirements in ISC Appendix O. Officials have the duties and powers set out in the ISC and Appendix V thereto.

topic: Article A5.7 - F1 Teams and PU Manufacturers Obligations
text: Each F1 Team and PU Manufacturer must satisfy the FIA, Stewards, and FIA Courts that they comply with all FIA F1 Regulations at all times. They must ensure Personnel are: informed and made aware of FIA Rules and their applicability; trained regarding their areas of responsibility and compliance impact; informed of the FIA ethics and compliance hotline; informed that personal devices used for work are not excluded from potential Demands; and informed upon joining that possession of materials from a previous employer is forbidden. F1 Teams must implement reasonable measures to prevent disclosure of Confidential Information to other teams. No F1 Team may use personnel movement to circumvent this requirement. Personnel covered include those involved in F1 Car design, research and development, simulation methodology development, and race operations or strategy. F1 Teams must inform the FIA of all relevant personnel movements using the Appendix A6 form.

topic: Article A5.7.3 - Movement of Personnel Between F1 Teams
text: When two cooperating F1 Teams (Team A and Team B, e.g., under same ownership or sharing parts/testing) transfer personnel, Team A must impose a Garden Leave period of not less than three months (or maximum permitted by law if less). Team B must include contractual clauses requiring an undertaking to the FIA and Team A that the person has not retained copies of Team A's Confidential Information and will not disclose it. These requirements apply vice versa and in reverse if the person returns to Team A. For temporary secondments, Team A must place the person on Restricted Duties for not less than three months before and after the secondment. Restricted Duties means either a period of unpaid leave or reassignment to duties not exposing the person to the team's Confidential Information. Personnel failing to comply are personally liable; the relevant team is also strictly liable regardless of whether the personnel are Covered Persons.

topic: Article A5.7.4 - Movement of Personnel Between PU Manufacturers
text: Each PU Manufacturer must implement reasonable measures to prevent disclosure of intellectual property and Confidential Information to existing or prospective fuel/oil suppliers or to another PU Manufacturer. No PU Manufacturer may use personnel movement to obtain an intellectual property transfer or circumvent these requirements. Personnel covered include those involved in Power Unit design, research and development, and simulation methodology development. PU Manufacturers must inform the FIA of all relevant personnel movements at the end of each calendar quarter using the Appendix A6 template.

topic: Article A6 - Investigations, Right of Inquiry, and Notification of Breaches
text: The FIA may open and conduct investigations under the FIA F1 Regulations at any time, subject to the limitation period in Article A7.9. Stewards conduct investigations per their ISC powers; anti-doping investigations follow ISC Appendix A. An F1 Team or PU Manufacturer (Complainant) may submit a report alleging another team's breach; the report must be submitted in Good Faith and promptly, identify the non-complying party, specify relevant provisions, include sufficient valid evidence, be signed by the CEO or Team Principal and the competent director, and be accompanied by a non-refundable administrative fee of €10,000 and a deposit of €40,000. The deposit is returned only if the complaint results in the FIA alleging a breach or no investigation is opened. The Complainant must keep their report confidential. The FIA notifies the subject in writing; if a report was filed by a Complainant, the FIA also notifies the Complainant of the decision to open or not open an investigation and may provide a summary to the subject. There is no right of appeal against a decision to open or not open an investigation.

topic: Article A6.2 to A6.4 - FIA Ethics Hotline, Information Requests, and Demand Powers
text: The FIA ethics and compliance hotline enables individual whistleblowers to raise confidential issues about alleged breaches. The FIA may make written requests to F1 Teams, PU Manufacturers, Key Individual F1 Team Members, or Key Individual PU Members for information, documentation, clarification, or access to premises and individuals. The FIA may, during investigations, issue Demands: written requests to access Electronic Devices (including smartphones, tablets, computers, portable hard drives, USBs, pagers, iWatches, messaging platforms, social media accounts, and cloud-based services) where it has reasonable grounds to believe data evidencing non-compliance may exist. Failure to comply with an FIA request constitutes a breach of Section A, unless Applicable Laws prevent compliance. Prior to formally charging, the FIA issues an Initial Notice, gives the Covered Person an opportunity to respond, and if a breach is concluded, issues a Final Notice and either seeks a settlement/ABA or escalates to the relevant FIA Court.

topic: Article A7.1 to A7.3 - Adjudication: Case Resolution, First Instance, and Appeal
text: Cases may be resolved without a hearing through a settlement agreement (Prosecuting Body) or Accepted Breach Agreement (Cost Cap Administration for Financial Regulations breaches); there is no appeal right on the decision whether to offer or enter an ABA or settlement. First-instance adjudication: Stewards appointed for an Event have supreme authority for enforcement within that Event; they may delegate to subsequent Event Stewards, the Out-of-Competition Stewards Panel, or recommend International Tribunal referral. The International Tribunal is competent in all first-instance disciplinary matters except anti-doping and Financial Regulations matters. The Cost Cap Adjudication Panel is competent in first-instance Financial Regulations disciplinary matters. The Anti-Doping Disciplinary Committee has exclusive competence for anti-doping matters. Appeals go to the International Court of Appeal (ICA) for Stewards, International Tribunal, and Cost Cap Adjudication Panel decisions. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has exclusive competence for appeals against Anti-Doping Disciplinary Committee decisions.

topic: Article A7.4 to A7.6 - Referral Procedures, ICA Appeals, Protests
text: Alleged Stewards breaches are referred to and heard by the Stewards. Alleged breaches of FIA F1 Regulations by Covered Persons are referred to the International Tribunal or (for Financial Regulations) the Cost Cap Adjudication Panel. Once referred, a Judging Panel is appointed. Appeals to the ICA: final decisions by Stewards, International Tribunal, or Cost Cap Adjudication Panel may be appealed; to be valid, notice of appeal must include a non-refundable administrative fee of €5,000 for F1 Teams, PU Manufacturers, or Drivers (€1,000 for other individuals) and a deposit of €20,000 for F1 Teams, PU Manufacturers, or Drivers (€6,000 for others). Appealed sanctions are not enforceable pending outcome unless the ICA orders otherwise or the decision is immediately binding per ISC Article 12.3.3. Protests require a deposit of €20,000. Right of Review petitions also require a €20,000 deposit.

topic: Article A7.9 - Limitation Period
text: The statutory limitation period for prosecuting offences or infringements is five years. The period runs from the date of the offence or infringement; for Financial Regulations (F1 Teams), from the later of the Full Year Reporting Deadline for the relevant period or the date the Cost Cap Administration learned of concealed acts or omissions. For successive or repeated offences, the period runs from the last act. For continuous offences, from the date it ceased. Where an offence has been concealed from the FIA, the limitation period runs from the date the FIA became aware. The limitation period is interrupted by any notice of prosecution or investigation under Chapter 2 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules. Anti-doping rule violations are subject to separate provisions in ISC Appendix A. The statute of limitations is classified as a procedural rule and is applied retroactively (unless the period had already expired at 1 January of Year N).

topic: Article A7.10 to A7.12 - Burden of Proof, Evidence, and Sanctions
text: The FIA bears the burden of establishing that a breach occurred. The standard of proof is comfortable satisfaction of the Judging Panel bearing in mind the seriousness of the allegation — greater than balance of probability but less than beyond reasonable doubt. Where the FIA F1 Regulations place the burden on the Covered Person, the standard is balance of probability. Liability is strict unless specified otherwise. No formal rules of admissibility apply; facts may be established by admissions, testimony, documentary or audiovisual evidence, data analysis, or reliable metadata. Failure to produce documents, appear at hearings, or respond to questions may result in adverse inference. Sanctions include general ISC sanctions plus additional Championship-specific sanctions: enhanced monitoring; withholding or cancellation of FIA registrations/licences; removal of right to access Reserved Areas; and suspension from participation in FIA or ASN competitions, preparatory testing, or F1 Activities. Sanctions may be suspended subject to conditions. Provisional suspensions may be imposed; non-compliance is an aggravating factor. Aggravating factors include failure to cooperate, bad faith, dishonesty, wilful concealment, fraud, prior breaches, multiple breaches, and severity. Mitigating factors include voluntary disclosure, track record of compliance, Force Majeure, and full cooperation.

topic: Article A7.12.8 and A7.13 to A7.14 - Financial Penalty Payment, Costs, and Immunity
text: Financial Penalties are paid per ISC Article 12.8; payments are suspended pending appeals. Delay in payment automatically removes the right to participate in the Championship until paid; late payments accrue interest of 2% above the US Federal Reserve federal funds rate on the due date. Costs of investigations and proceedings are determined by the Judging Panel per FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules. The FIA may grant partial or total immunity to persons who disclose breach facts or provide prosecutable evidence; the degree of immunity depends on whether the FIA already had the information, the extent of cooperation, case importance, nature of breach, and past conduct. Immunity grants must be in writing, signed by both parties, specify the nature and extent of immunity, and set out which sanctions will not be imposed. Immunity conditions require ongoing full cooperation, truthfulness, and non-destruction of evidence. Immunity is irrevocable if conditions are met; the FIA may seek revocation if conditions are not met. Revocation decisions are not subject to appeal.

topic: Article A8 - Confidentiality, Public Reporting, and Data Privacy
text: Information received by the FIA, Stewards, and FIA Courts may be shared among those bodies for regulatory purposes, with external specialists under confidentiality obligations, and with competent authorities where required by law. The FIA may publicly report: investigation openings and outcomes; notifications of alleged breaches; case referrals to Stewards or FIA Courts; final decisions; appeal filings and hearing dates; ICA final decisions; ABA or settlement agreement summaries; Financial Regulations compliance status; and names of Key Individual F1 Team Members, Key Individual F1 PU Members, and Drivers. For Financial Regulations breaches by natural persons, public reporting occurs only after final appeal decisions, expiry of appeal rights, or conclusion of ABA or settlement agreements. International Tribunal and ICA hearings are open to media and public unless the Hearing President decides otherwise, except for Financial Regulations matters. Teams may publicly comment on FIA-reported information but may not disclose other enforcement-related information. Breaches of confidentiality by teams or their representatives constitute a breach of Section A. The FIA processes personal data per the FIA Motorsport Privacy Notice at www.fia.com/motorsport-privacy-notice.

topic: Article A9 - Effective Period, Amendments, Interpretation
text: The FIA F1 Regulations come into force on 1 January 2026 and apply to the entire calendar year and Championship within that year. Amendments must be approved by the WMSC per ISC Article 18 and must satisfy applicable governance processes. The FIA may make the following amendments with only WMSC approval (no advisory committee or F1 Commission approval required): safety amendments; deletion of redundant articles; updating year-specific date references; and correction of typographical or minor errors not affecting interpretation. The FIA F1 Regulations for each year are assumed identical to those of the previous year unless amended. The definitive version is the English version. The Regulations must be interpreted as independent and autonomous text; they are governed by French law. In case of conflict between Section A and Section E, Section E prevails on its subject matters. In all other conflicts between Section A and other Sections, Section A prevails. The Stewards, first-instance FIA Courts, and ultimately the ICA have final interpretive authority. All correspondence with the FIA must be in English. Only written communications (letter or email) from the FIA may be relied upon as the FIA's definitive position.

topic: Article A9.4.5 - Interpretation Rules
text: Unless specified otherwise: defined words and phrases (denoted by initial capital letters) have the meaning in Appendix A1 and apply to all Sections; headings are for ease of reference only; 'may' means sole and absolute discretion; words following 'including', 'such as', 'for example' are illustrative only; the pronoun 'they/their' is used for individuals and includes all genders; singular includes plural and vice versa (not applicable to provisions specifying technical characteristics, measurements, component quantities, or numerical limits); Articles and Appendices with alphabetical letter prefixes refer to that Section of the FIA F1 Regulations; references to provisions include modifications or successor provisions; 'writing', 'write', 'written' includes email; 'day' means any day of the week (not limited to working days); time refers to Central European Standard Time; time limits begin the day after notice is received; official holidays and non-working days are included in time limits except the last day; a 'person' (no initial capital) means a natural person. If any part of the Regulations is found illegal, invalid, or unenforceable, that part is deemed not to form part of the Regulations, and the remainder remains valid.

topic: Article A9.5 to A9.8 - Clarification Requests, Language, Reliance, Transitional Provisions
text: F1 Teams or PU Manufacturers may submit written requests to the FIA to clarify the operation or interpretation of the FIA F1 Regulations. Requests must include: a full description of the intended interpretation with drawings or calculations as appropriate; opinions on immediate and long-term implications on the Regulations and Championship; and how it will impact technical, sporting, financial, or operational performance. The FIA responds in writing with a full explanation. The FIA may circulate clarifications as FIA F1 Documents. Clarifications and feedback are advisory only and do not form part of the Regulations. All correspondence must be in English; the FIA may require certified translations of relied-upon documents. Only written FIA communications (letter or email) may be relied upon as the FIA's definitive position. Transitional provisions: periods prior to Year N are governed by substantive rules in effect at that time; procedural rules apply retroactively. Pending cases as of 1 January of Year N and charges for pre-Year-N breaches are governed by substantive rules in effect at the time of the breach, unless 'lex mitior' applies.

topic: Appendix A1 - Key Definitions (A-F)
text: Accepted Breach Agreement (ABA): agreement between FIA and F1 Team, PU Manufacturer, or Declaration Signatory per Article 7.1.2 and Financial Regulations. Advisory Committee: committee operating under F1 Commission mandate, covering Technical (TAC), Sporting (SAC), Financial (FAC), and PU (PUAC) Regulations. ASN: national club, association, or federation recognised by FIA as sole holder of Sporting Power per FIA Statutes Article 3.3. Automotive Manufacturer: manufacturer of at least one automobile model produced in at least 3,000 units in the past 12 months. Championship: the FIA Formula One World Championship including both Constructors' and Drivers' Championships. Circuit: closed course beginning and ending at the same point, built or adapted for automobile racing; may be temporary, semi-permanent, or permanent. Circuit Operator: entity responsible for operating a Circuit, holding a Circuit licence issued by the FIA. Commercial Rights Holder: holder of exclusive right to exploit commercial rights in the Championship, being Formula One World Championship Limited. Competition: race meeting forming part of the Championship commencing four hours before the first practice session to the deadline for lodging a Protest or completion of technical/sporting certification. Competition Number: number assigned to F1 Drivers and Other Racing Drivers per Article A2.4. Constructor: person or body that designs Listed Team Components or outsources their design/manufacture. Cost Cap: meaning in relevant Financial Regulations. Cost Cap Administration: FIA-designated staff to administer and monitor Financial Regulations. Covered Person: each person covered by Article A1.3.2.

topic: Appendix A1 - Key Definitions (F-L)
text: F1 Activities: all activities by or on behalf of F1 Teams related to Championship participation including research, development, design, manufacture, Testing, racing, and marketing of F1 Cars; and all activities by or on behalf of PU Manufacturers including research, development, design, manufacture, assembly, Testing, supply, servicing, and marketing of Power Units. F1 Car: car designed and built to comply with Technical Regulations of Year N or Year N-1; referred to as 'Automobile' in the ISC. F1 Commission: commission with competence over all Championship matters including amendments to FIA F1 Regulations. F1 Driver: person engaged by a Reporting Group Entity whose primary role is racing F1 Cars in the Championship during Year N and who has driven in a race. F1 Team: legal entity holding an FIA Super Licence to participate in the Championship (also referred to as Competitor or Constructor in the ISC). FIA: Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile, global governing body of motorsport. Force Majeure: circumstances beyond reasonable control including terrorist action, civil commotion, invasion, war, fire, explosion, storm, flood, earthquake, natural disaster, epidemic, pandemic, and legislation or ruling of any government or court. Garden Leave: period during which personnel changing employer is isolated from Confidential Information or F1 Activities; may involve carrying out unrelated work within the previous employer's Legal Group. Key Individual F1 Team Member: each person required to be registered as key Personnel per Appendix A5 and ISC Article 2.6.4, and each Declaration Signatory. Legal Professional Privilege: covers communications between lawyer and client for the sole or dominant purpose of giving or receiving legal advice, or communications for the sole or dominant purpose of obtaining advice or information in connection with existing or contemplated litigation; applies to both external and in-house lawyers.

topic: Appendix A1 - Key Definitions (N-Z)
text: New Entrant PU Manufacturer: PU Manufacturer admitted to Championship but not yet participated. New Entrant Team: F1 Team admitted to Championship but not yet participated. Parc Fermé: designated secure area at a Competition where F1 Cars are kept after qualifying and during certain periods, with teams prevented from working except for FIA-permitted adjustments. Personnel: any person engaged in F1 Activities on behalf of the F1 Team or PU Manufacturer or their Legal Group, including Key Individual F1 Team Members and Key Individual PU Members. Power Unit (PU): internal combustion engine and turbocharger complete with ancillaries, energy recovery system, and all actuation systems and PU control electronics. Power Unit Manufacturer: legal entity that successfully completes FIA registration to be eligible to homologate Power Units for supply to F1 Teams. Restricted Duties: either unpaid leave where the person is not required to attend or perform duties, or reassignment to alternative duties not exposing the person to that team's Confidential Information. Safety Car: physical safety car brought onto the track to limit F1 Car speeds. Scheduled Race Distance: original Race distance in laps as specified on the Competition visa Circuit permit. Virtual Safety Car (VSC): safety measure to slow all F1 Cars without using a physical Safety Car. Witness: fact witness and/or expert witness. World Champion Constructor: F1 Team that most recently won the Constructors' Championship. World Champion Driver: F1 Driver who most recently won the Drivers' Championship. WMSC: World Motorsport Council constituted under FIA Statutes. Year N: calendar year in the title of the FIA F1 Regulations.

topic: Appendix A2 - Advisory Committees Summary
text: Advisory Committees discuss regulatory amendments and general topics leading to improvement of FIA F1 Regulations, subject to applicable governance processes. Each Advisory Committee is composed of one senior representative each from the FIA, the Commercial Rights Holder, F1 Teams (where appropriate), and Power Unit Manufacturers (where appropriate). The FIA chairs meetings and performs secretariat functions. Committees: RGAC (Regulatory and Governance Advisory Committee) covers Section A, attended by F1 Teams' Legal Director/Counsel; SAC (Sporting Advisory Committee) covers Section B, attended by F1 Teams' Sporting Director; TAC (Technical Advisory Committee) covers Sections C and F chassis matters, attended by F1 Teams' Technical Director; PUAC (PU Advisory Committee) covers Sections C and F PU matters, attended by PU Manufacturers' Technical Director; FAC (Financial Advisory Committee) covers Section D, attended by F1 Teams' Financial Director; PUFAC (PU Financial Advisory Committee) covers Section E, attended by PU Manufacturers' Financial Director; EAC (ESG Advisory Committee) covers environmental and sustainability matters, attended by F1 Teams' and PU Manufacturers' Sustainability Director.

topic: Appendix A3 - Access to Electronic Devices (Demands)
text: When the FIA makes a Demand, the F1 Team or PU Manufacturer must immediately (or by the FIA-specified deadline) make Electronic Devices available for inspection and copying/download, and provide Login Information (usernames, passwords, and any other means required to access data). If an objection to a Demand is raised, the devices must still be provided for securing/copying, but the FIA will not access the data until the objection is resolved by the Judging Panel. A Demand does not cover private Electronic Devices unless the team or PU Manufacturer agreed they could be used for work purposes. Refusal or failure to give access, or attempted or actual damage, alteration, destruction, or concealment of data constitutes a breach of Section A. Confidentiality is not a valid ground to refuse compliance; however, no obligation exists to disclose documents rendered confidential by court order or statute, documents not in the party's possession or control, or documents subject to Legal Professional Privilege. Teams must ensure confidentiality obligations in their contracts are made subject to the FIA's right of inquiry. F1 Teams and PU Manufacturers waive rights to withhold Electronic Devices on privacy grounds. Parties may take ten days to seek legal advice before the FIA reviews data, provided device integrity is preserved. Objections to Demands are filed with the relevant Judging Panel within seven days; one Judging Panel member considers the matter expeditiously. The Judging Panel ruling on a Demand may not sit on subsequent related disciplinary panels. Judging Panel rulings under this Appendix are not subject to appeal and are not published.

topic: Appendix A4 - Entry Form for Championship and Registration Form for Key Personnel of F1 Teams
text: The Entry Form requires: full company name, country of incorporation, company registration number, date of incorporation, country of residence, registered office, trading address, contact details, directors, Team Principal, Team Manager, and authorised representatives. Constructor's Details require: national licence number, issuing body, team name (including chassis name), make of F1 Car, make of Power Unit, and names of both F1 Drivers (or indication of subsequent nomination). Technical Partner Details: a Technical Partner must be a Related Party of the F1 Team, can only be a Technical Partner to a single team, must be declared on the entry form and approved by the FIA, and the F1 Team is responsible for the Technical Partner's compliance. Declarations confirm reading and agreeing to all FIA Rules, awareness of Data Protection and Privacy Notice, accuracy of provided information, and undertaking to pay the Entry Fee by 15 December of Year N-1. The Registration Form for Key Personnel requires signatures from: CEO, CFO, Team Principal, Sporting Director, Technical Director, Team Manager, Race Engineer (1), and Race Engineer (2). Each must confirm compliance with FIA Rules and consent to personal data processing.

topic: Appendix A5 - Registration Form for Key Personnel of PU Manufacturers
text: The PU Manufacturer registration form requires: full company name, country of incorporation, company registration number, date of incorporation, country of residence, registered office, administrative headquarters, and technical headquarters. Key Personnel to be registered include: CEO, CFO, Technical Director, Technical Representative, Chief Engineer, Head of Trackside Engineering, Head of Customer Engineering (for each Customer F1 Team if different from Head of Trackside Engineering), PU Engineer for F1 Car 1, PU Engineer for F1 Car 2, and PU Engineers for Customer F1 Cars (N = 2 x number of Customer F1 Teams supplied). Each person must confirm compliance with FIA Rules and Regulations and consent to personal data processing. The form must be signed by a duly authorised representative of the PU Manufacturer.

topic: Appendix A6 - Movement of Personnel Form
text: The Movement of Personnel Declaration form is used per Articles A5.7.3 and A5.7.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations. The form requires: Team or PUM name; date; reporting period (from-to); submitted by; and submitter's position. Section 1 covers personnel leaving the F1 Team or PU Manufacturer: number, name, position in organisation, leaving date, isolation date (if any), destination (if known), and notes. Section 2 covers personnel joining the F1 Team or PU Manufacturer: number, name, future position in organisation, arrival date, isolation date (if any), origin, and notes.

topic: Appendix A7 - Supply of Power Units: Registration and Obligations
text: Any entity wishing to supply Power Units for 2026-2030 must complete the PU Manufacturer registration form, enter into the PU Manufacturer Non-Assert Agreement, and enter into the 2026 F1 PU Governance Agreement. The registration deadline for Year N is the later of: 30 June of Year N-4; 30 days after the first publication of 2026 PU Technical, Sporting, and Financial Regulations; or 15 October 2022. Registration acceptance is at the FIA's sole discretion; late registration may be accepted if no competitive or financial advantage was gained. Registration is only complete upon payment of the administrative fee, entry into the PU Manufacturer Non-Assert Agreement, and agreement to governance processes. Each PU Manufacturer must provide the FIA by 15 May of Year N-1 with the list of Competitors for Year N, clearly identifying the appointed works/factory Competitor. The works/factory Competitor is the one belonging to the PU Manufacturer's Legal Group Structure, or if none exclusively, the one with the highest Constructors' Championship position in Year N-2. A PU Manufacturer called upon by the FIA before 1 June of Year N-1 must supply at least T Competitors, calculated as T = (NTOT-A)/(B-C) where NTOT=11. No PU Manufacturer may supply more than (T+1) teams. A PU Manufacturer wishing to cease supply must notify the FIA by 1 January of the preceding year.

topic: Appendix A7 - New Customer Competitor Supply Conditions
text: A PU Manufacturer is required to supply a New Customer Competitor if requested by the FIA unless the competitor already has a supply agreement or binding offer. Supply must be on substantially the same terms as those with Existing Customer Competitors, except price. If no Existing Customer Competitors, the PU Manufacturer determines payment terms at sole discretion (subject to price limits). Supply contract duration: not less than one Championship season; not more than three Championship seasons, nor beyond 2030, unless jointly agreed. The PU Manufacturer determines whether the New Customer Competitor uses the PU Manufacturer's name or a white label. Neither party shall make disparaging or negative comments about the other. Key conditions the New Customer Competitor must meet: no binding contracts with another PU manufacturer for the supply period; not be an Automotive Manufacturer set up to participate in the Championship; no sponsorship in competition with the PU Manufacturer's Core Activities; key executives/directors/shareholders must not appear on EU/US sanction lists, have criminal convictions for specified offences, have been declared bankrupt, or have committed reputationally harmful actions. The maximum PU supply price for 2026 is €22 million (adjusted for Indexation as per Appendix 1 of the Formula 1 Power Unit Financial Regulations), decreasing to €20.75 million for 2027. Payment falls back to four instalments: 25% on signature; 25% by 30 October of Year N-1; 30% before Championship start; 20% before the fifth Event.

topic: Appendix A7 - Fuel and Oil Supply Obligations and Non-Exclusivity
text: Fuel and/or engine oil suppliers for 2026-2030 must: complete the supplier registration form by 1 January of Year N-1; pay FIA invoices per FIA-F1-DOC-004 Sustainable Fuel Certification Programme; agree to be bound by ISC, Technical Regulations, Sporting Regulations, and FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules; agree to the Non-Assert Agreement; agree to FIA jurisdiction. The Prospective Supplier Non-Assert Agreement prohibits suppliers from asserting patents or licensed rights against the FIA, Commercial Rights Holder, other suppliers, PU Manufacturers, and Competitors in connection with fuel/engine oil used in Formula 1 during 2026-2030. PU Manufacturers must nominate their Prospective Suppliers within 90 days of registration. Certain information cannot be shared between PU Manufacturers and Fuel/Oil Suppliers, including combustion chamber drawings, CAD files, physical parts, and information on gas exchange (except cylinder pressure data, simulation, and dyno test results). No PU Manufacturer may use personnel movement to obtain intellectual property transfer between itself and fuel/oil suppliers. With the exception of fuel/engine oil agreements, no PU Manufacturer may enter exclusive supply agreements that prevent equally advantageous supply of components or technology to another PU Manufacturer. Patents, pending applications, or licensed rights of a PU Manufacturer shall not prevent other PU Manufacturers from using any technology, design, or concept in their PUs in Formula 1; PU Manufacturers must enter into the PU Manufacturer Non-Assert Agreement.

topic: Appendix A7 - New PU Manufacturer Status
text: A PU Manufacturer supplying PUs for the first time in Year N is a New PU Manufacturer if it (or any related party): has not homologated a PU at least once in the period 2014-2021; and has not received significant recent Intellectual Property from a non-New PU Manufacturer. New PU Manufacturer status is granted by the FIA at absolute discretion for calendar years N-3 to N+1, and gives additional rights and exemptions in Technical, Sporting, and Financial Regulations. To assess qualification, the FIA evaluates: Infrastructure (40% weight in Financial Regulations, 20% in Technical/Sporting); ICE status (50% Financial, 50% Technical/Sporting); ERS status (10% Financial, 30% Technical/Sporting). For Technical/Sporting Regulations, New PU Manufacturer status is awarded in full if the sum is at least 50%, otherwise at zero. Partial New PU Manufacturer status may be granted if the FIA determines the Necessary Conditions are not fully satisfied. The FIA may revoke the status if information provided has changed significantly or new evidence shows erroneous information was provided. Knowingly providing false or misleading information is a material breach. If New PU Manufacturer status is awarded, the FIA communicates this to all other PU Manufacturers with a detailed report including percentage scores and reasons, omitting confidential information. There is no right of appeal against FIA decisions on New PU Manufacturer status.

topic: Appendix A8 - Championship Trophy Rules
text: The Constructors' Trophy and Drivers' Championship Trophy (FIA Trophies) may not be used or displayed to suggest commercial association between the FIA and any third party, and must not be used in any manner that brings the Championship, FIA, Commercial Rights Holder, or motorsport into disrepute. The FIA Trophies are presented at the FIA Prize Giving Ceremony and Gala Dinner to the World Champion Constructor and World Champion Driver. The trophies are engraved with the champion names for the relevant year prior to the start of the following Championship. For the Constructors' Trophy: the World Champion Constructor is entitled to possession for a period determined by the FIA, then receives a replica to keep. The constructor must insure the trophy for the FIA-advised insured value, maintain it appropriately, and return it in the same condition. If not returned in the same condition, the constructor is liable for repair, restoration, or replacement costs. The FIA may request the trophy at any time on 14 days' notice, meeting reasonable transport charges. The constructor pays transport charges during its possession. The World Champion Driver receives only a replica of the Drivers' Championship Trophy to keep.

topic: Appendix A9 - Approved Changes to Section A for Subsequent Years
text: Approved changes for 2027 affect Appendix A7, Article 1.4 (Power Unit maximum supply price): the PU supply price for the PU supply perimeter listed in the corresponding column of Appendix C4 changes from €22 million (2026) to €20.75 million (2027), adjusted for Indexation per Appendix 1 of the Formula 1 Power Unit Financial Regulations. Additional goods or services not listed in the Appendix incur additional charges based on market usages and practices. No changes are approved for 2028, 2029, or 2030.
